name: CO2 Cylinder Pro
summary: Refillable aluminium CO2 cylinders with standard CGA-320 valves, from a cabinet-friendly 2.5 lb up to 20 lb. Bigger cylinders mean fewer trips to the refill station.
highlights: Standard CGA-320 valve for Pro and Mini regulators
bestFor: Anyone running a Pro or Mini regulator who wants the lowest running cost per fill.
watchOut: Ships empty, and must be hydrostatically tested every five years before it can be refilled in the US.

name: CO2 Diffuser
summary: A clear acrylic in-tank diffuser with a white ceramic disc that breaks CO2 into a fine mist of bubbles. Acrylic makes it harder to break than the usual glass diffusers.
highlights: Three sizes by tank volume: Small, Medium, Large
Ceramic disc diameters of 12, 17 and 24 mm
Transparent acrylic, less fragile than glass
bestFor: Any pressurised CO2 tank where you want a simple, low-cost in-tank diffuser.
watchOut: Discs clog over time and need a soak in diluted bleach to restore fine bubbles.

name: CO2 Paintball Cylinder
summary: Small refillable aluminium cylinders that sit between disposable cartridges and full-size bottles. The built-in on/off valve makes swapping them safer than a pin-valve paintball tank.
highlights: Pairs with the UNS Mini Dual Stage regulator
bestFor: Small to medium tanks where a full-size cylinder will not fit in the cabinet.
watchOut: Needs a paintball adapter on the regulator (one comes with the Mini Dual Stage).

name: Drop Checker
summary: A glass drop checker that changes colour with the CO2 level in your tank, giving you an at-a-glance check that injection is in the right range. It comes in a hang-on style for rimless tanks and a suction-cup style for anything else.
highlights: HD hangs over rimless glass up to 10 mm thick
SD fixes inside the tank with a suction cup
bestFor: Anyone running pressurised CO2 who wants a simple visual check.

specs.Included: 15 ml indicator solution

extra.Fits: Rimless tanks with glass up to 10 mm

watchOut: Drop checkers lag the tank by an hour or two, so read them late in the photoperiod.

name: Micro CO2 Bubble Counter
summary: A small detachable bubble counter with a check valve built in. It lets you see and set your bubble rate while stopping water from running back into the regulator.
highlights: Fits the UNS Micro, Mini and Pro regulators
Clear body for easy bubble counting
bestFor: Fine-tuning bubble rate on any UNS regulator, or as a spare.

specs.Compatible with: UNS Micro, Mini Dual Stage and Pro Dual Stage regulators

name: Micro CO2 Kit
summary: The smallest complete pressurised CO2 setup UNS makes. It pairs the Micro regulator, solenoid and bubble counter with a 95 g disposable cartridge on a stand, so a nano tank can run on a timer without a big cylinder in sight.
highlights: Micro regulator, Micro solenoid and bubble counter included
Runs on 95 g disposable CO2 cartridges
Cartridge stand, tubing and diffuser included
Small enough to sit beside a desktop tank
bestFor: Nano and desktop planted tanks where you want timed, pressurised CO2 on a small budget.

specs.Included: Regulator, solenoid, bubble counter, cartridge, stand, tubing, diffuser

watchOut: Disposable cartridges cost more per gram than a refillable cylinder, so it gets expensive on bigger tanks.

name: Micro CO2 Regulator
summary: A pocket-sized aluminium regulator that screws onto UNS disposable cartridges. On its own it is a manual regulator; add the Micro solenoid and bubble counter (sold together as the Regulator Kit) to put it on a timer.
highlights: Made for UNS 95 g disposable cartridges
Modular: add the Micro solenoid and bubble counter
Also sold as a Regulator Kit with solenoid and bubble counter
bestFor: Desktop nanos where every centimetre of space around the tank counts.

extra.Includes: Micro regulator, Micro solenoid, Micro bubble counter

watchOut: It only takes disposable cartridges, so you cannot move it to a refillable cylinder later.

name: Micro CO2 Solenoid
summary: The add-on solenoid for the Micro regulator. Plug it into a timer and your CO2 switches on and off with the lights instead of running all night.
highlights: Fits the UNS Micro CO2 Regulator
Compact block that keeps the Micro setup small
bestFor: Anyone already running the Micro regulator who wants CO2 on a schedule.
watchOut: It only fits the Micro regulator; the Mini and Pro regulators already have a solenoid built in.

name: Mini CO2 Dual Stage Regulator
summary: A compact dual-stage regulator with a built-in solenoid that works with three gas sources out of the box: disposable cartridges, paintball cylinders and full-size CGA-320 cylinders. It grows with you if you move to a bigger tank.
highlights: Dual stage, so no end-of-tank dump as the cylinder empties
CGA-320 adapter fitted, paintball adapter included
bestFor: Nano and small tanks, especially if you might switch from cartridges to a refillable cylinder later.

specs.Cylinder: CGA-320, paintball (adapter included) and UNS disposable cartridges
specs.Included: CGA-320 adapter, paintball adapter, bubble counter, power adapter, spare o-rings, tools

watchOut: It has a single gauge, so you get less warning of an empty cylinder than with the Pro's two gauges.

name: Nano CO2 Kit
summary: A cartridge-based kit built around the Mini Dual Stage regulator. You get the stability of a dual-stage regulator with a built-in solenoid, but in a size that fits beside a small tank.
highlights: Mini Dual Stage regulator with built-in solenoid
95 g disposable cartridge on a stand
Regulator can later move to a paintball or full-size cylinder
bestFor: Tanks of roughly 4 to 40 litres where you want dual-stage stability without a large cylinder.

specs.Included: Regulator, cartridge, stand, CO2 tubing, diffuser

watchOut: A cartridge lasts around two to three months on a small tank, so running costs add up compared with refilling.

name: Paintball CO2 Kit
summary: The Mini Dual Stage regulator paired with a refillable paintball cylinder. It holds a lot more gas than a cartridge but still fits in a small cabinet, which makes it a sensible middle step.
highlights: Mini Dual Stage regulator with built-in solenoid
16 oz or 24 oz refillable paintball cylinder
Cylinder has its own on/off valve
bestFor: Small to medium planted tanks where cartridges run out too fast but a full-size cylinder will not fit.

specs.Included: Regulator, cylinder, CO2 tubing, diffuser

watchOut: The cylinder ships empty, so you need a local refill source before you can start.

name: Pro CO2 Dual Stage Regulator
summary: A full-size dual-stage regulator with two gauges, a built-in solenoid and two bubble counter manifolds. Add more manifolds and one cylinder can feed several tanks.
highlights: Dual stage with working and cylinder pressure gauges
Two bubble counter manifolds included, expandable to about eight outputs
For CGA-320 cylinders from 2.5 to 20 lb
bestFor: Medium to large planted tanks and fish rooms running refillable cylinders.

specs.Included: CGA-320 adapter, 2 bubble counter manifolds, power adapter, spare o-rings, tools

watchOut: It is bulky and only takes CGA-320 cylinders, so it is overkill for a single nano.

name: Pro CO2 Kit
summary: A full-size refillable CO2 system: a UNS Pro cylinder with the Pro Dual Stage regulator (the 2.5 lb kit uses the Mini regulator). It is the long-term option, with fewer refills and room to split gas across several tanks.
highlights: Pro Dual Stage regulator with two gauges and bubble counter manifolds
Standard CGA-320 fittings, refillable at gas and welding suppliers
bestFor: Medium to large high-tech tanks, or several tanks fed from one cylinder.

specs.Regulator: UNS Pro CO2 Dual Stage (Mini Dual Stage on the 2.5 lb kit)
specs.Included: Regulator, cylinder, CO2 tubing, diffuser

watchOut: Cylinders ship empty and need hydrostatic testing every five years in many regions.

name: Pro Inline CO2 Diffuser
summary: An inline diffuser that fits in your canister's outflow hose, so CO2 is dissolved before the water reaches the tank and nothing extra sits in the scape. The ceramic disc is side-mounted, which keeps flow restriction down and makes it easy to swap.
highlights: Keeps diffuser clutter out of the tank
12 mm fits Delta 60/90 and Blitz 32 oz; 16 mm fits Delta 120
bestFor: Canister-filtered CO2 tanks where you want a clean, equipment-free look inside the glass.
watchOut: It needs a canister with enough flow, and the disc will need cleaning or replacing now and then.

name: C Series Chiller
summary: Compact inline chillers for home aquariums, using R-134a refrigerant and a microprocessor thermostat. Three sizes cover roughly 50 to 600 litres. Worth a look if summer heat pushes your tank past what fans can handle.
highlights: Three sizes for about 50 to 600 L
bestFor: Planted tanks and shrimp tanks in hot climates that regularly creep above safe temperatures.
watchOut: Chillers dump heat into the room and need a pump or canister to push water through them.

name: CW / LN Series Chiller
summary: Big box chillers for very large aquariums and fish rooms, rated from 500 up to 3,000 litres. Boyu lists the CW and LN codes with identical specs, and the LN range adds a 2 HP model.
bestFor: Very large display tanks or multi-tank systems in warm climates.
watchOut: They use R-22 refrigerant, which is phased out in many countries, so check local servicing rules before buying.

name: FS Series Cooling Fan
summary: Clip-on fans that blow across the water surface to cool the tank by evaporation. The range runs from the small FS-55 and single 120 mm FS-120 to the FS-600 bars with two to six fans in a row.
highlights: Mostly 12 V DC; FS-120 also in mains
Multi-fan bars (FS-602 to 606) for long tanks
bestFor: Cheap, low-power summer cooling for small and medium tanks that only run a couple of degrees too warm.
watchOut: Evaporative cooling means you will top up water more often, and fans only knock off a few degrees.

name: LS Series Chiller
summary: A vertical chiller with a titanium heat exchanger and a digital temperature display. The plain models also include a heater, so one unit can hold temperature both ways; the A versions are cooling only.
highlights: Digital display and push-button set point
Non-A models add a 300 to 450 W heater
bestFor: Keepers who want year-round temperature control from one box on a medium to large tank.
watchOut: Rated flow through the unit is low (400 to 600 L/h), so check it matches your pump.

name: Cooling Fan (Bluetooth Edition)
summary: A clamp-on stainless fan that blows across the water surface to pull temperature down by evaporation. The Bluetooth version lets you set speed, a target temperature and a schedule from your phone.
highlights: Bluetooth control of speed, temperature and schedule
Clamps on glass up to 19 mm
bestFor: Planted and shrimp tanks that creep too warm in summer or under strong lights.

specs.Mounting: Rim clamp, glass up to 19 mm

watchOut: Evaporative cooling means topping up more often, and it only shaves a few degrees compared with a chiller.

name: climacontrol+
summary: climacontrol+ is an inline unit that both chills and heats, controlled over WiFi. It sits on the return line after your canister, holds a set temperature anywhere from 5 to 35 °C and e-mails you if things go wrong.
highlights: Cools and heats in one inline box
Set and monitor temperature over WiFi
Warning e-mail if the water is off target for 5 minutes
bestFor: Big planted tanks in warm rooms or hot climates where summer temperatures push past 28 °C.
watchOut: It is expensive, needs 500 to 800 L/h of clean filtered water through it and wants 5 cm of clear space around it for airflow.

name: HYH-D Aquarium Chiller
summary: The smallest units in SunSun's HYH chiller range, with 250 to 650 W of cooling for tanks around 260 to 580 litres. They take 16 to 20 mm hose and use R134a refrigerant.
bestFor: Tanks in hot rooms or with cool-water species that climb above safe temperatures in summer.

specs.Bigger units: HYH DR models cover 600 to 4,500 litres

watchOut: Chillers need a pump or canister to push water through and dump heat into the room, so give them ventilation.

name: APT Balance
summary: Beneficial bacteria designed for aquasoil tanks. Dosed into a new or unsettled tank, it speeds up nitrification so ammonia and nitrite clear faster in the early weeks.
bestFor: New aquasoil tanks during cycling, or after a big rescape or filter clean.
watchOut: Bacteria still need a source of ammonia and time, so keep testing during the cycle.

name: APT Dew
summary: A balanced macro, micro and trace fertiliser in a spray bottle, applied to leaves instead of the water. For aquarium keepers it is most useful during the dry-start method, before a tank is flooded.
highlights: Foliar spray with macro, micro and trace nutrients
Feeds plants grown out of water
bestFor: The dry-start phase of a carpet, and emersed mosses and plants above the waterline.
watchOut: It is a spray for leaves out of water, not a fertiliser to dose into the aquarium.

name: APT Feast
summary: A nutrient-rich aquasoil that feeds roots and softens the water. 2HR rates it for a sustained boost of up to about 12 months, with pH settling around 6.2 to 6.6.
highlights: Feeds roots for up to around a year
bestFor: New planted tanks and soft-water shrimp setups that want a feeding substrate from day one.
watchOut: Like most rich aquasoils it releases ammonia at first, so cycle the tank before adding livestock.

name: APT Fix
summary: A spot treatment for stubborn algae, especially black beard, staghorn and the stringy or fuzzy filamentous types. You dose it straight onto the algae with the flow off, and it biodegrades.
bestFor: Planted tanks with patches of black beard algae or hair algae on hardscape and slow plants.

specs.Treats: BBA, hair, string, fuzz and most filamentous algae

watchOut: It can harm mosses, liverworts and vallisneria. Use APT FixLite in tanks with those plants, and fix the cause of the algae too.

name: APT FixLite
summary: A gentler version of APT Fix for tanks with mosses, liverworts such as riccardia and riccia, vallisneria and other delicate plants that full-strength treatments can knock back.
highlights: Safer around mosses, liverworts and vallisneria
bestFor: Moss-heavy and delicate-plant tanks that still need to tackle algae.
watchOut: Being gentler, it can take more applications than full-strength APT Fix.

name: APT Jazz
summary: Slow-release capsules pushed into the substrate that feed roots with substrate-bound ammoniacal nitrogen and other macros. It works alongside a liquid fertiliser rather than replacing it.
highlights: Substrate-bound nitrogen and macros for root feeders
Designed to be used with 2HR's liquid fertilisers
bestFor: Swords, crypts, lilies and other heavy root feeders, especially in older aquasoil or inert gravel.

specs.Supplies: Ammoniacal nitrogen and macros at the roots
specs.Sizes: Mini (9 caps), Small (18 caps), Large (54 caps)

watchOut: Push capsules deep into the substrate; shallow placement can leak nutrients into the water.

name: APT Pure
summary: A concentrated dechlorinator for water changes. It removes chlorine and chloramine and binds ammonia, nitrite and heavy metals, with aloe vera added.
highlights: Detoxifies ammonia, nitrite and heavy metals
bestFor: Anyone doing water changes with tap water.

name: APT Sky
summary: A remineraliser that puts calcium, magnesium and other minerals back into RO or RODI water without raising KH, pH or adding NPK. It lets shrimp and hard-water plants thrive alongside soft-water plants.
highlights: Restores GH in RO and RODI water
Does not raise KH or pH
No added nitrogen, phosphorus or potassium
bestFor: Soft-water planted tanks and Caridina shrimp tanks started from RO water.

specs.How often: Every water change with RO water
specs.Sizes: Mini (70 g), Small (150 g), Large (800 g)

watchOut: It is for RO or RODI water; adding it to hard tap water will push GH higher than you want.

name: APT Sky Plus
summary: Like APT Sky, it remineralises RO or RODI water without adding NPK, but it also raises KH to about 2 dKH and pH to around 7.2 to 7.6. That suits Neocaridina and harder-water plants.
highlights: Restores GH in RO and RODI water
Raises KH to about 2 and pH to 7.2 to 7.6
No added nitrogen, phosphorus or potassium
bestFor: RO-water tanks keeping Neocaridina shrimp or plants that prefer a little buffering.

specs.Effect on KH and pH: Raises KH to about 2, pH to 7.2 to 7.6
specs.How often: Every water change with RO water

watchOut: Not for Caridina or very soft-water setups, since it raises KH and pH.

name: APT Start
summary: A one-off booster for new tanks that combines substrate enrichment with starter bacteria. It adds organics and nutrients that help the first cycle settle faster.
highlights: Helps a new tank cycle faster
bestFor: Brand-new tanks at the planting stage, before the tank is flooded or filled.
watchOut: It is a setup product, so it does not replace ongoing fertiliser dosing.

name: APT1
summary: The same micro and trace nutrients as APT3, with no added nitrate or phosphate. It is for tanks where fish waste already supplies plenty of nitrogen and phosphorus.
highlights: Micro and trace nutrients plus potassium
Pairs with a heavy fish load
bestFor: Well-stocked tanks where nitrate already reads high, or where you dose nitrogen separately.

specs.How often: Daily or several times a week
specs.Sizes: Starter, Standard, 200 ml, 500 ml, 600 ml, 1000 ml

watchOut: In a lightly stocked tank plants can run short of nitrogen and phosphorus on APT1 alone.

name: APT3
summary: A liquid fertiliser that covers macro, micro and trace nutrients in one bottle, so a single daily dose replaces mixing separate products. It is 2HR's default choice for a planted tank with CO2 and a normal fish load.
highlights: Macro, micro and trace nutrients in one bottle
One product to dose, no dry salts to mix
2HR's balanced ratio aimed at strong growth and good red colour
bestFor: CO2-injected planted tanks with an average fish load that want one simple fertiliser.

specs.Supplies: Macro (N, P, K), micro and trace
specs.How often: Daily or several times a week
specs.Sizes: Starter, Standard, 200 ml, 500 ml, 600 ml, 1000 ml

watchOut: If nitrate keeps building up because of a heavy fish load, APT1 (no nitrate or phosphate) is the better fit.

name: APTe (APT EI)
summary: A ready-mixed take on the Estimative Index method: generous, non-limiting doses of every nutrient, reset by a big weekly water change. It gives you the EI approach without weighing out dry salts.
highlights: Based on the Estimative Index dosing method
No dry salts to weigh or mix
bestFor: Fast-growing, high-light CO2 tanks where you do a large water change every week.

specs.Supplies: Macro, micro and trace at EI levels
specs.How often: Daily, with a large weekly water change

watchOut: EI relies on weekly water changes of about half the tank to stop nutrients building up, so it is not for low-tech tanks.

name: Bottom Plus
summary: Slow-release root sticks pushed into the substrate next to root-feeding plants. They release nutrients gradually over several months without affecting the water much.
bestFor: Swords, crypts, vallisneria and other root feeders, especially in older or inert substrate.
watchOut: Push sticks fully under the substrate; exposed sticks can leach nutrients and feed algae.

name: ECA Plus
summary: A concentrated iron and sulphur additive for tackling chlorosis, where new leaves turn pale or yellow. It works faster than routine dosing and is used when plants already show symptoms.
bestFor: Tanks where new growth has gone pale or yellow from an iron shortage.
watchOut: It is a corrective, concentrated product; dose carefully rather than as a daily fertiliser.

name: Green Brighty Iron
summary: A liquid iron supplement from ADA's Green Brighty range, for vigorously growing plants that use a lot of iron. It is dosed alongside ADA's other Green Brighty bottles rather than on its own.
highlights: Part of ADA's modular Green Brighty range
bestFor: Fast-growing and red plants showing pale new growth from low iron.

specs.How often: Regularly, with other Green Brighty bottles

watchOut: Pale new leaves are not always iron. Check the deficiency guide first so you do not overdose one nutrient.

name: Green Brighty Mineral
summary: ADA's trace element supplement, supplying the minor nutrients plants need for healthy new buds and pigment. It is the trace part of the Green Brighty system.
highlights: Supports new bud growth and colour
bestFor: Planted tanks of any tech level that need trace elements topped up.

name: Green Brighty Neutral K
summary: A potassium supplement that does not raise pH or KH. ADA recommends it where tap water is already high in pH and KH, and for plants that prefer softer conditions.
highlights: Does not raise pH or KH
Suits harder tap water and soft-water plants
bestFor: Tanks with pinholes in older leaves from low potassium, especially with hard tap water.

specs.Suits: Hard tap water and soft-water plants

name: Green Brighty Nitrogen
summary: ADA's nitrogen supplement, used to keep leaf colour strong and growth steady in tanks where plants use up nitrogen faster than fish produce it.
bestFor: Heavily planted, lightly stocked tanks where older leaves yellow from low nitrogen.
watchOut: Skip or reduce it in well-stocked tanks where nitrate already reads high.

name: Green Gain Plus
summary: A plant supplement based on seaweed-derived plant hormones, trace elements and amino acids, with boron for new buds. It is used to help plants recover from trimming and stress.
highlights: Trace elements, amino acids and boron
bestFor: Freshly trimmed or newly planted tanks where you want faster regrowth of new shoots.

specs.Supplies: Plant hormones, amino acids, trace, boron
specs.Contains: Plant hormones, trace elements, amino acids, boron

watchOut: It supports growth rather than supplying the main nutrients, so use it with a regular fertiliser.

name: DGN-410 / 460 / 520 Canister Filter
summary: A 24 V canister with a brushless DC pump, so you can wind the flow up or down instead of choking it with a tap. All three sizes share the same pump and footprint; the bigger numbers just add height and media space. The plain versions carry a 3 W UV lamp, the A versions leave it out.
highlights: Variable pump: 300 to 1,610 L/h at 4 to 30 W
Runs off an external 24 V adaptor
Same 24 x 24 cm footprint across all three sizes
3 W UV lamp on non-A models
bestFor: Mid to large planted tanks where you want to tune flow to the scape without swapping filters.

specs.Variants: Standard (with 3 W UV) or A (no UV)

watchOut: The flow figure is shared across the range, so the larger bodies buy you media volume rather than extra flow.

name: DGN-80 / 120 UVC Canister Filter
summary: A newer, white-bodied canister with a UVC lamp built in and a one-button prime. It comes in two sizes, each offered with or without the A suffix. Handy if green water has been a recurring headache, though a planted tank with good balance rarely needs UV running all the time.
highlights: Built-in UVC lamp with its own on/off switch
One-button air purge and siphon start
Clamp-lock lid and hidden carry handle
bestFor: Medium to large community tanks where the owner wants mechanical, biological and UV treatment in one box.
watchOut: Power draw is high for the flow (35 W and 55 W including the UV), and Boyu does not publish a recommended tank size.

name: EF / EFU Canister Filter
summary: A no-frills external canister in six sizes, with shut-off valves built into the in and out ports so you can disconnect it for cleaning without draining hoses. The EFU versions are the same bodies with a 5 W UV lamp added. Flow ratings are modest, so treat the maker's tank ranges as generous.
highlights: Integrated shut-off valves on the head
EFU models add a 5 W UV lamp
bestFor: Budget-minded keepers with 100 to 650 litre tanks who want canister filtration and optional UV.

specs.Valves: Built-in taps on inlet and outlet

watchOut: The rated tank ranges are optimistic for a planted tank; size up if you want strong circulation.

name: FEF-230 / 280 Canister Filter
summary: A squarer canister with a built-in UV steriliser on its own switch and a valve block on the head for easy disconnection. Two sizes, each in two finishes. Flow is healthy for the power it uses.
highlights: Built-in UV with a separate switch
Valve block on the lid for quick disconnection
bestFor: Medium tanks around 150 to 300 litres where a budget UV canister makes sense.
watchOut: Boyu does not state the UV wattage or a recommended tank size.

name: SP-C / SP-B Internal Filter
summary: A submersible pump head sitting on one or two slotted sponge cartridges, which makes a simple internal filter that also aerates through a venturi. It is the classic cheap internal: effective at mechanical cleaning, easy to rinse, but bulky in a small scape.
highlights: Pump plus one or two sponge cylinders
Venturi air intake for extra oxygen
bestFor: Quarantine, hospital or grow-out tanks, and simple community tanks that need an easy internal filter.
watchOut: It is large and very visible in the tank, and the maker lists the SP-2300B with the same 8 W and 300 L/h as the small model, which looks like a sheet error.

name: WF Waterfall Hang-on Filter
summary: A simple hang-on-back filter that returns water as a wide waterfall, which keeps the surface moving and breaks up oily film. There are five sizes, from a tiny 150 L/h unit up to 720 L/h. Cheap and easy to service, but the splash does drive off CO2.
highlights: Layered media basket in the hang-on box
Surface skimming built in on the larger WF-2035 to 2055
bestFor: Small to medium low-tech tanks and shrimp or betta setups on a budget.
watchOut: The waterfall return gases off CO2, so it is not ideal on an injected tank, and Boyu gives no recommended tank sizes.

name: 950F Series Internal Filter
summary: A powerhead sitting on top of a slotted strainer tube packed with sponge. The bigger 970F and 980F push a lot of water for an internal filter.
bestFor: A larger tank that needs strong extra circulation plus some mechanical filtration.
watchOut: The larger sizes are bulky and strong for a planted tank; they can flatten stem plants and are hard to hide.

name: A Series Hanging Filter
summary: A chunky hang-on-back filter with adjustable flow, an extendable intake and a media-change reminder dial. It comes either with an open media box (sponge, carbon, bio balls) or a carbon cartridge.
highlights: Choice of open media box or carbon cartridge version
bestFor: A 40 to 100 litre tank where you want a simple hang-on filter you can fill with your own media.

specs.Versions: Media box (sponge, carbon, bio balls) or carbon cartridge

watchOut: Get the media box version for a planted tank, so you can skip carbon; like all hang-on filters the waterfall return drives off some CO2.

name: C Series Canister Filter
summary: A tall, square brown canister line from C-500 to C-1600 with a push-button primer and double valve taps. The number of media baskets grows from two to five as you go up the range.
highlights: Push-button primer and double shut-off taps
Spray bar and intake strainer included
bestFor: A 100 to 190 litre planted tank on a budget where you want room for plenty of your own media.

specs.Media supplied: Carbon, quartz rings, black sponge, white wool (varies by size)

watchOut: The flow ratings are for the bare pump; packed with media and hoses the real flow is well below that, though still generous for the listed tank sizes.

name: CF Series UV Canister Filter
summary: A grey canister range from a 410 L/h mini up to the big 3000 L/h C2400, with most sizes offered with an internal UV lamp. The mid sizes share their ratings with the CF688 range in a different body.
highlights: UV lamp of 5 to 9 W on UV versions
CF300 mini canister for small tanks
bestFor: Anyone wanting a cheap canister with optional UV, from a 40 litre shrimp tank (CF300) to a large display (C2400).

specs.UV: Optional on CF600 to C2400 (UV suffix models); CF300 has no UV

watchOut: UV does nothing for algae growing on plants and can reduce some chelated trace elements if left on all the time; the C2400 is a big unit that needs cabinet space.

name: CF11008 Series CO2 Canister Filter
summary: A squared-off canister with two planted-tank extras built in: a CO2 inlet that mixes gas from your cylinder into the filter flow, and a bay that holds a standard glass heater inside the head. Three sizes rated 950 to 1450 L/h.
highlights: CO2 inlet and mixing chamber in the filter, cylinder not included
Internal bay for a 22 to 24 mm heater keeps the tank clear of kit
bestFor: A budget planted tank of roughly 60 to 140 litres where you want CO2 and heating hidden inside the filter.

specs.CO2: Built-in inlet and mixing system; connect your own cylinder and regulator
specs.Heater bay: Takes a 22 to 24 mm diameter heater (not included)

watchOut: The maker warns to turn the CO2 off before unplugging, or water can back up out of the CO2 tube; as with any filter-mixed CO2, some gas can collect in the canister.

name: CF2000 Pre-Canister Filter
summary: A small canister that sits in the intake line before your main filter and catches the muck first. It has its own media holder and a drain valve, so you empty the pre-filter often and open the main canister far less.
highlights: Traps debris before it reaches the main canister
bestFor: A planted tank with lots of leaf litter or trimmings where you are tired of stripping down the main canister.

specs.Pump: None, runs on your main canister's flow

watchOut: It has no pump of its own, adds another hose run and some flow resistance, and must be kept clean or it will choke the main filter's flow.

name: CF688 Series Canister Filter
summary: A round blue canister range from 800 to 1400 L/h, each size available with or without a built-in UV lamp (the UV versions add a UV suffix). The UV sits inside the canister behind a safety switch.
highlights: Optional internal UV lamp of 5 to 9 W
Spray bar, lily-style inlet/outlet pipes and directional spout included
bestFor: A 60 to 140 litre tank that suffers green water now and then, where a UV option in the same box saves buying a separate unit.

specs.UV: Optional; UV models are CF688UV, CF888UV, CF1288UV, CF1488UV (uvW applies to these)

watchOut: UV only kills free-floating algae and microbes, not algae on leaves, and running it constantly can break down some chelated trace elements, so many planted-tank keepers only switch it on when needed.

name: F Series Internal Filter
summary: A tall, slim internal filter in three sizes with a blue flow-adjust knob on top; the small F-800 can take a rain bar.
bestFor: A mid-sized tank where you want an internal filter that tucks into a back corner.
watchOut: Like any internal box it takes up room in the scape and holds less media than a canister.

name: FB Internal Filter
summary: A plain rectangular internal filter with a sponge body and a side outlet that can take a rain bar. Four sizes cover roughly 50 to 140 litres.
highlights: Rain bar option for spread flow
bestFor: A basic community or planted tank where a simple sponge internal filter is enough.
watchOut: Media volume is small, so it needs rinsing often in a heavily stocked tank.

name: FC Filter Box
summary: Slim box-shaped internal filters with the pump at the bottom and a waterfall-style outlet at the top. Most use a drop-in sponge and carbon cartridge, and the range runs from tiny nano sizes up to the tall FC-601.
highlights: Low-mounted pump pulls from near the substrate
Drop-in cartridge, so no wet hands
bestFor: A small desktop or nano tank that needs a compact, cheap internal filter.

specs.Media: Sponge and carbon cartridge (FC-601 uses layered media)

watchOut: Cartridges are an ongoing cost, and the waterfall outlet splashes, which is poor for CO2; for planted tanks swap the carbon for plain sponge once it is spent.

name: H Series Hanging Filter
summary: A classic smoked-grey hang-on-back range from the tiny H-80 to the 1000 L/h H-800. Each uses a bio cartridge plus a carbon cartridge that needs changing periodically.
bestFor: A beginner tank from 25 to 200 litres where a familiar, easy hang-on filter is enough.
watchOut: The carbon cartridge is a running cost and strips some liquid fertiliser, so planted-tank keepers often swap it for sponge.

name: KF Internal Filter
summary: Very small internal filters, only 8 to 9.5 cm tall, with an adjustable outlet nozzle. The KF-160 is the slimmest of the four.
bestFor: A nano or shrimp tank of 30 to 70 litres that needs a tiny, cheap internal filter.
watchOut: The intake is not shrimp-safe as supplied, so cover it with a sponge in a breeding tank.

name: Power Head Top Filter
summary: A long plastic filter tray that sits across the top of the tank, fed by a submersible powerhead. Four lengths fit tanks from about 47 cm up to 127 cm.
highlights: Tray lengths to suit 47 to 127 cm tanks
bestFor: An older-style framed tank without a lid where you want a lot of cheap, easy-to-clean media.
watchOut: A top filter blocks part of the tank top, clashing with most planted-tank lights, and its trickle return drives off CO2.

name: SH Slim Hanging Filter
summary: A slim hang-on-back filter only 5 cm deep, with the motor down on the intake tube and a floating surface skimmer built into the intake. Sizes differ mainly in how many standard carbon cartridges they hold.
highlights: Only 5 cm deep behind the tank
Built-in floating surface skimmer clears surface film
bestFor: A 20 to 80 litre tank with a lid-free top where you want surface film gone without a separate skimmer.

specs.Cartridges: One standard size across the range

watchOut: The cartridges contain carbon, which you may prefer to replace with sponge in a fertilised planted tank, and the spill-over outlet gasses off some CO2.

name: TF Internal Filter
summary: A tall corner-style internal filter that comes with a spray bar, so the return can be spread along the back of the tank instead of blasting one spot.
highlights: Slim profile for the back corner
bestFor: A 50 to 150 litre tank where you want gentle, spread-out flow without a canister.
watchOut: Internal filters take up visible space in the scape, and the media capacity is small next to a canister.

name: aqua Corner Filter
summary: The aqua is a slim internal filter shaped to sit in a back corner, which leaves more open space for the scape. Filter modules clip together, so you can add another cartridge later if you need more capacity, and there is a small media box for carbon or bio media.
highlights: Corner shape keeps it out of the way of your layout
Clip-in modules, expandable with extra cartridges
Media box takes carbon, SUBSTRATpro or similar
Adjustable output and a diffuser included
bestFor: Beginner planted tanks of roughly 100 to 200 litres where you want something simple that hides in a corner.

specs.Includes: Foam cartridges, 20 g carbon, diffuser and hose

watchOut: The listing does not give a flow figure, so on a CO2 tank you may want a separate circulation pump to be safe.

name: Aquaball
summary: The Aquaball is an internal filter with a ball-joint pump head, so you can point the outflow wherever you want surface movement. Foam cartridges handle mechanical and biological filtration, and there is a venturi if you want to add air.
highlights: Swivelling ball head for aiming the outflow
Adjustable flow, 480 to 650 L/h at the top end
Modular baskets, one to three depending on size
Venturi diffuser for extra oxygen when you need it
bestFor: Small to medium low-tech planted tanks, or as a backup filter and circulation boost on a bigger tank.
watchOut: Switch the venturi off on a CO2 tank, as the bubbles will drive off the gas you are paying for.

name: Biopower
summary: Biopower takes the Aquaball pump head and adds closed baskets filled with SUBSTRATpro, so it behaves more like a small canister hung inside the tank. It comes with a spray bar and a venturi, and the flow is adjustable.
highlights: Closed baskets of SUBSTRATpro for more biological capacity than a sponge filter
Spray bar included for gentle surface movement
bestFor: Medium planted tanks without room for a canister, or tanks with a heavier fish load that need more biology than a basic internal.
watchOut: It is a tall column inside the tank, so plan your hardscape to hide it.

name: Classic
summary: The Classic is the round green canister that has been running on aquariums for decades. It is one open chamber you fill with whatever media you like, with no prefilter tray, electronics or clever valves to go wrong. Simple, quiet and very hard to kill.
highlights: Single open canister, so you choose and layer the media yourself
Low running costs: 8 to 20 W depending on size
Very few moving parts, so long-term reliability is its strong point
Spare parts and replacement pads are easy to find almost anywhere
bestFor: Keepers who want a no-fuss, long-lived canister for a planted tank and are happy to do a slightly messier clean now and then.

specs.Media: Supplied with pads or loose media depending on pack

watchOut: Priming is manual on the basic version and there is no quick-release tap block, so cleaning takes more effort than on newer Eheim lines.

name: classicVARIO+e
summary: This is the old Classic canister rebuilt with a brushless, WiFi-controlled pump. You set the flow from a browser, and it can ramp down at night or during feeding if paired with other Eheim digital kit. It is quiet and sips power.
highlights: Brushless DC pump, adjustable in fine steps
Manual and pulse modes, set over WiFi
Uses as little as 1.7 W at low flow
Maintenance reminder by e-mail when cleaning is due
bestFor: Planted tanks of about 50 to 250 litres where you want a silent, simple canister with adjustable flow and do not need a big media load.
watchOut: Flow tops out around 510 L/h, which is modest for a high-tech tank at the top of its size range.

name: Ecco Pro
summary: Ecco Pro is Eheim's compact entry canister, sized for small and mid-sized tanks. The carry handle doubles as the lever that locks the head and primes the filter, and media sits in stacked baskets, so cleaning is tidy. Power draw is very low.
highlights: Built-in priming via the handle lever, no sucking on hoses
Stacked media baskets plus a small prefilter make cleaning quick
12/16 mm hoses on all three sizes, which suits slim lily pipes
bestFor: Planted tanks from about 60 to 300 litres where you want an easy canister that tucks into a small cabinet.

specs.Media: Supplied complete with pads, SUBSTRATpro and hoses

watchOut: Flow is modest for the rated tank sizes, so on a heavily planted CO2 tank choose a size up or add a circulation pump.

name: Experience
summary: The Experience range sits between the Classic and the Professionel. You get a square canister with media baskets and a double-tap hose block with a single release lever, so you can close both valves and lift the filter out without spilling.
highlights: Square canister is stable and packs neatly into a cabinet
Two adjustable shut-off valves on a quick-release adaptor
Supplied with mechanical and biological media, ready to run
350 model steps up to 16/22 mm hoses and over 1,000 L/h
bestFor: Mid-sized planted tanks where you want easier maintenance than a Classic without paying Professionel money.

specs.Taps: Double tap adaptor with release lever

watchOut: The 150 and 250 are fairly gentle on flow, so on a high-tech tank you may want the next size up.

name: miniFLAT
summary: The miniFLAT lies flat on the bottom rather than hanging on the glass, so it works in very shallow water. It draws water in from underneath, passes it through a sponge and pushes it out of the top, which keeps a small water area moving.
highlights: Works in water only a few centimetres deep
Sticks to the floor with suction cups
Hose connection lets you aim the outflow, for example into a small stream
bestFor: Very shallow nano tanks and low water levels that still need a bit of filtration and movement.
watchOut: It is a tiny sponge filter, so it will not keep up with a stocked aquarium on its own.

name: Pick-up
summary: Pick-up filters are small sponge internals that stick to the glass with suckers. The motor stays put while the sponge housing slides off for rinsing, so you do not have to unclip the whole thing or wrestle the cable.
highlights: Filter body slides off the motor for cleaning
Carbon sponge available if you want it
bestFor: Nano and small planted tanks, quarantine or shrimp tanks where a canister would be overkill.
watchOut: Media volume is tiny, so biological capacity is limited and the sponge needs rinsing often on a well-fed tank.

name: Professionel 3 1200XL
summary: The 1200XL (type 2080) is Eheim's big canister for very large tanks. It holds 12 litres of media plus a 1.5 litre prefilter, has two intake connections and one outlet, and rolls on built-in wheels because it is heavy once full.
highlights: 12 L of media plus a large 1.5 L prefilter
Two inlet connections and one outlet, all 16/22 mm
Flow and maintenance indicator on the head
Wheels and recessed handles for moving it around
bestFor: Very large planted displays, roughly 600 litres and up, where one filter needs to carry a lot of media.
watchOut: Media is not included, it draws 45 W and is over 56 cm tall, so check cabinet height before you buy.

name: Professionel 4+
summary: The Professionel 4+ is Eheim's mechanical flagship canister, with a lift-out prefilter under the head, separate media baskets and a self-priming pump. The Xtender button reroutes water past clogged fine pads so the biology keeps running until you get round to cleaning. The 250T and 350T versions add a 210 W heater inside the canister.
highlights: Top prefilter catches debris so the main media stays cleaner for longer
Xtender button buys a few extra days when flow starts to drop
Thermo versions (250T, 350T) hide a 210 W heater in the filter, freshwater only
16/22 mm hoses on every model, with a safety tap adaptor
Quiet ceramic shaft and adjustable flow
bestFor: Planted tanks from about 120 to 600 litres where you want solid flow, long service intervals and, if you like, no heater in the display.

specs.Water type: Freshwater and marine (thermo models freshwater only)
specs.Media: Supplied complete with Eheim media and fittings

watchOut: It is a tall, fairly heavy canister, so measure your cabinet, and the thermo models are not for marine use.

name: Professionel 5e
summary: The 5e is the electronic version of the Professionel, with a brushless pump you set up over WiFi from a browser. It can hold a constant flow as the media clogs, run a pulse mode, or drop to a quieter night flow. The 600T adds a built-in 210 W heater for freshwater tanks.
highlights: Constant-flow mode tops up pump speed as the media gets dirty
Day and night flow settings, plus pulse mode, all via WiFi in a browser
Up to 1,850 L/h with 8 L of media plus a 0.6 L prefilter on the big models
Links with Eheim's other digital kit, for example pausing flow at feeding time
600T thermo version has a 210 W heater inside, freshwater only
bestFor: Larger high-tech planted tanks where you want strong, adjustable flow and like the idea of tuning it from your phone.

specs.Control: WiFi via web browser, no app needed

watchOut: It costs a lot more than the 4+, and the WiFi setup is web-based rather than a polished app, which not everyone enjoys.

name: Bioflow
summary: The large internal box filter built into Juwel aquariums, also sold on its own. Water runs down through stacked sponges and media baskets, with space for a Juwel heater inside the housing and an Eccoflow pump on top. There are no hoses, so nothing can leak outside the tank.
highlights: Three sizes: M (3.5 L media), L (8 L), XL (11 L)
600 or 1,000 L/h Eccoflow pump using 7 to 8 W
Room for a Juwel AquaHeat heater inside the filter
Five media stages supplied: poly pad, carbon, Nitrax, coarse and fine sponges
bestFor: Juwel owners replacing or upgrading a filter, or anyone happy with a big internal box in exchange for no hoses.
watchOut: It takes up a noticeable slice of the back corner and needs a tank at least 42.5 cm (M) or 60 cm (L, XL) tall.

name: BioCompact
summary: A very small internal filter for nano and quarantine tanks. It can be mounted upright or on its side, which makes it handy in shallow water, and the flow is adjustable at the outlet. The 50 has a media chamber you can refill with whatever you like.
highlights: Two sizes for tanks up to 25 or 50 litres
Adjustable flow of roughly 120 to 240 L/h
Can be installed horizontally for shallow water
bestFor: Nano tanks, shrimp tanks and quarantine tanks where space is tight.
watchOut: Tiny media capacity means frequent rinsing, and it is visible in the tank.

name: BioMaster 2
summary: Oase's main canister filter, built around a pre-filter module you lift out and rinse without opening the whole canister. Water passes through foam first, so the Hel-X biological media behind it stays clean for much longer. A heater can be retrofitted later, and there is a Thermo version with one already fitted.
highlights: Five sizes for tanks from 150 to 850 litres
Pre-filter lifts out for a quick rinse without opening the canister
3 to 8 litres of media including Hel-X
Priming button and auto shut-off valves make restarts easy
bestFor: Medium to large planted tanks where you want long gaps between full cleans and easy weekly pre-filter rinses.

specs.Pre-filter: EasyClean removable pre-filter module, 30/45 ppi sponges
specs.Safety: Automatic shut-off valve when the pre-filter is removed
specs.Thermo versions: Available with a built-in heater (models marked Thermo), which keeps the heater out of the tank

watchOut: Rated flow drops once hoses, lily pipes and media are fitted, so size up for a heavily planted tank.

name: BioPlus
summary: A corner internal filter with a built-in, adjustable outlet nozzle instead of a separate spray bar. The media unit unclips and lifts out while the pump stays put, which makes cleaning quick. Foam plus a fine fleece stage gives decent polishing for its size.
highlights: Three sizes for tanks up to 50, 100 or 200 litres
Media unit lifts out for cleaning, pump stays in place
Fits neatly in a rear corner with suction cups
bestFor: Small to mid-sized tanks where you want a simple internal filter that is easy to service.

specs.Thermo versions: Available with a built-in heater (models marked Thermo), which keeps the heater out of the tank

watchOut: It sits inside the tank, so it takes up scaping space and needs hiding behind plants or hardscape.

name: BioStyle
summary: A hang-on-back filter from Oase that hooks over the rim, so there are no hoses and nothing takes up space inside the tank. It uses a drop-in cartridge with foam, fleece and carbon, and a telescopic clear intake adjusts to your tank depth. Flow is generous for the size, which suits small tanks with light fish loads.
highlights: Three sizes for tanks up to 70, 115 or 180 litres
Cartridge change indicator and simple swap-out media
Adjustable spacers for a secure fit on the rim
bestFor: Small planted tanks or shrimp tanks where you want easy filtration without a canister or an internal box.

specs.Mounting: Hangs on the tank rim, adjustable spacers

watchOut: Hang-on filters splash at the surface, which drives off some CO2 in an injected tank.

name: FiltoSmart
summary: A compact, budget-friendly canister from Oase for small and mid-sized tanks. It has a self-venting start, shut-off valves on the connectors and an EasyClick lid, and it comes complete with media, hoses and pipes. The smallest model is a genuinely tiny canister that suits nano tanks.
highlights: Four sizes for tanks from 60 to 300 litres
FiltoSmart 60 is small enough for a nano cabinet or beside the tank
Self-venting start-up and shut-off valves for spill-free cleaning
Flow adjustable at the inlet and outlet adapters
bestFor: Nano to mid-sized planted tanks where you want a quiet canister without paying BioMaster money.

specs.Supplied with: Media, hoses, adapters, intake and outflow pipes, spray diffuser
specs.Thermo versions: Available with a built-in heater (models marked Thermo), which keeps the heater out of the tank

watchOut: Media volume is modest on the 60 and 100, so they need cleaning more often than bigger canisters.

name: AF-260 Top Filter
summary: A top-mounted filter box for tanks 30 to 60 cm long that sits on the rim and takes 14/16 mm hose from a pump. It gives a small tank a trickle-style media box without a sump.
bestFor: Small fish tanks where you want extra media above the water.
watchOut: Trickle boxes vent CO2, so it is not ideal for an injected planted tank.

name: CBG Hang-On Filter with UV
summary: A hang-on-back filter with an oil-film surface skimmer, double flow regulation and a built-in 5 W UV-C lamp (S models skip the UV). Two sizes for 38 to 190 litre tanks.
bestFor: Small to mid planted tanks that suffer from surface film or green water.
watchOut: UV kills free-floating algae but will not fix algae on plants or glass; the root cause still needs sorting.

name: CF Series Internal Filter Pump
summary: A simple internal filter pump in three sizes, 350 to 900 L/h. The same basic design as SunSun's HQJ pumps with a filter body.
bestFor: Small fish tanks.

name: CHJ-02 Series Internal Filter
summary: CHJ pumps fitted with a clear media column, from 500 to 1,500 L/h. Handy as a simple all-in-one internal filter.
bestFor: Small and mid fish tanks.

name: CUP-800 UV Internal Filter
summary: A compact internal filter pump with a UV-C lamp, rated for tanks from 250 to 750 litres depending on the lamp size. Flow is 700 L/h on all four models.
bestFor: Mid to large tanks with green water problems.
watchOut: Flow is modest for the tank sizes quoted, so treat it as a UV unit rather than main filtration on big tanks.

name: HBL Series Hang-On Filter
summary: SunSun's long-running hang-on-back filters, from the tiny 2 W HBL-301 up to the larger adjustable-flow HBL-800 range. They are cheap, simple and easy to service.
highlights: HBL-801 to 803 have adjustable flow and fit different glass thicknesses
Used in several SunSun tank kits
bestFor: Nano and small planted tanks, shrimp tanks and quarantine setups.
watchOut: Hang-on filters break the surface and can drive off CO2, and the intake needs a sponge cover in a shrimp tank.

name: HJ-42 Series Internal Filter Pump
summary: SunSun's HJ submersible pumps fitted with a sponge filter chamber, from 400 to 3,000 L/h. They can filter a tank on their own or push water through a separate filter.
bestFor: Small to large fish tanks and temporary setups.
watchOut: The bigger models make strong, noisy flow for their size; the small ones suit planted tanks better.

name: HJ-B Series Mini Internal Filter
summary: Tiny internal filters from 200 L/h, plus a few larger HJ-5x2 models up to 1,200 L/h. Several are used in SunSun's desktop tanks.
bestFor: Pico, nano and small tanks.

name: HN Internal Filter
summary: A slim 3 W internal filter for small tanks, with 300 L/h flow. Two heights.
bestFor: Nano and small tanks up to about 40 litres.

name: HQJ-I and HQJ-S Internal Filter
summary: Internal filters with a sponge column and pump head, from 300 to 500 L/h. S models add a taller filter section.
bestFor: Small fish tanks and quarantine tanks.

name: HW-300 and HW-400 Series Canister Filter
summary: The classic SunSun canisters (HW-302, 303, 304 and the 400-series equivalents), with a pre-filter tray and optional UV-C lamp on B models. They have been a common budget choice for planted tanks for years.
bestFor: Budget-conscious keepers with 100 to 500 litre planted tanks.

extra.Variants: HW-303A without UV, HW-303B with 5, 7 or 9 W UV-C
HW-304A without UV, HW-304B with 5, 7 or 9 W UV-C
HW-402A without UV, HW-402B with 5, 7 or 9 W UV-C
HW-403A without UV, HW-403B with 5, 7 or 9 W UV-C
HW-404A without UV, HW-404B with 5, 7 or 9 W UV-C

watchOut: The pumps draw more power (18 to 55 W) than newer DC canisters, and the stock hoses are fairly stiff.

name: HW-3000 Series Frequency Canister Filter
summary: SunSun's variable-speed canister, with a touch display that steps the pump through six or seven flow levels and a built-in 9 W UV-C lamp. An oil-film skimmer comes with it to clear surface scum.
highlights: 1,200 to 4,600 L/h depending on model and setting
bestFor: Large planted or community tanks (roughly 200 litres and up) where adjustable flow is useful.

specs.Control: LED touch screen for flow and UV timer
specs.Included: Surface skimmer

watchOut: These are big units (up to 55 cm tall and 10.5 kg on the HW-5000), so check your cabinet height first.

name: HW-500 Series Canister Filter
summary: An older SunSun canister range with rotating in/out connections, from small 320 L/h models up to the 1,000 L/h HW-507. B versions of the 504, 505 and 507 add a UV-C lamp.
highlights: UV-C on B versions (5 or 9 W)
bestFor: Small to mid planted tanks where you want a simple canister.

extra.Variants: HW-504A without UV, HW-504B with 5 W UV-C
HW-505A without UV, HW-505B with 9 W UV-C
HW-507A without UV, HW-507B with 9 W UV-C

watchOut: SunSun does not list flow or head for the HW-504 and HW-505.

name: HW-600 Series Mini Canister Filter
summary: A small canister for nano and small tanks, sold with a separate pump (B models) or as a bare filter body. Flow is 400 to 800 L/h.
highlights: Bare versions let you use your own pump
bestFor: Nano and small planted tanks, 30 to 100 litres, that want canister filtration.

extra.Variants: HW-602 sold without pump
HW-603 sold without pump
HW-604 sold without pump

name: HW-700 Series Canister Filter
summary: A three-size canister range from 1,000 to 2,000 L/h, each sold as an A version (no UV) or B version with a 9 W UV-C lamp. It is SunSun's current take on the popular HW-300 series.
bestFor: Mid to large planted tanks, roughly 150 to 500 litres, on a budget.

extra.Variants: HW-702A without UV, HW-702B with 9 W UV-C
HW-703A without UV, HW-703B with 9 W UV-C
HW-704A without UV, HW-704B with 9 W UV-C

watchOut: Budget canisters vary in seal quality; check the lid O-ring when setting up and after cleaning.

name: JF Biochemical Sponge Filter
summary: A twin sponge filter driven by a small 3 W electric pump instead of an air pump, in three widths. It gives gentle flow and a big sponge surface for bacteria.
bestFor: Shrimp tanks, fry tanks and small planted tanks that need gentle, safe filtration.

name: JP-09 Series Internal Filter
summary: Three internal filters with a spray bar on the outlet, from 250 to 650 L/h. Low wattage (3 to 7 W).
bestFor: Small tanks where you want gentle, spread-out return flow.

name: JP-F Series Internal Filter
summary: SunSun's JP submersible pumps with tall sponge filter columns attached, from 300 to 1,600 L/h. The JP-02x/B versions are the same pumps with a short intake strainer instead.
bestFor: Small to mid fish tanks.

name: JS Three-in-One Top Filter
summary: A rim-mounted top filter box with its own pump, whose support arms extend to fit different tank widths. Two sizes, 350 and 650 L/h.
highlights: Adjustable arms (24 to 41 cm, or 41 to 61 cm)
Filter box sold separately as JS-400B/600B
bestFor: Small to mid fish tanks that want easy-access top filtration.
watchOut: Like any trickle filter, it drives off CO2 and splashes more than a canister.

name: JUP UV Internal Filter
summary: An internal filter with a UV-C lamp built into the body, from 500 to 800 L/h. Lamp sizes run from 5 to 13 W.
bestFor: Tanks fighting green water that want the UV inside the tank.
watchOut: UV clears green water but will not fix nutrient or light problems causing algae on plants.

name: XBA Clip-On Filter
summary: A very small 2.5 W clip-on filter with an activated carbon plate, for tanks under 40 cm. Flow is up to 300 L/h.
bestFor: Pico and nano tanks, betta setups.
watchOut: Carbon removes liquid fertiliser too, so swap it for sponge in a planted tank.

name: XBL Hang-On Filter
summary: A small hang-on filter from SunSun's Xiaoli line, in four sizes for tanks up to 30, 40, 50 and 60 cm. Flow is 300 or 500 L/h.
highlights: Sized by tank length (30 to 60 cm)
bestFor: Nano and small tanks under 60 cm.

name: XN Low Water Level Filter
summary: An internal filter built to work in shallow water, with one, two or three stacked media sections. Every size runs the same 10 W, 800 L/h pump.
bestFor: Shallow tanks and low water levels where a normal internal filter would suck air.

name: XQP-F Internal Filter
summary: The Xiaoli-line version of SunSun's filter pumps, with a filter box on the intake, from 500 to 1,500 L/h. The same pumps are sold bare as the XQP water pumps.
bestFor: Small to mid tanks.

name: XWA Series External Filter
summary: An external filter from SunSun's Xiaoli line with stacked media trays (three or five tiers) and an optional 9 W UV-C lamp. Flow runs from 500 to 1,400 L/h.
bestFor: Small to mid tanks where you want lots of media volume in a compact external box.

extra.Variants: 3 or 5 media trays; U versions add 9 W UV-C
3 or 5 media trays; U versions add 9 W UV-C
3 or 5 media trays; U versions add 9 W UV-C

name: Blitz Stainless Steel Filter
summary: A tiny canister filter with a brushed stainless steel body and matching steel pipes. It is made for nano tanks where a plastic canister would look out of place, and it runs quietly on low wattage.
highlights: Two sizes: 6 oz (tanks up to about 10 L) and 32 oz (up to about 45 L)
Stainless steel canister with matching inflow and outflow pipes
6 oz runs from USB; 32 oz uses a 12 V supply
bestFor: Nano and desktop tanks where the filter sits on show next to the aquarium.

specs.Included: Canister, steel inflow and outflow pipes, clear tubing, power cable, tool, foam mat

watchOut: Media capacity is small, especially on the 6 oz, so expect to clean it more often than a bigger canister.

name: Delta Canister Filter
summary: A compact white canister range that covers everything from a 5N nano to a 120 cm tank. Version 2 ships with Aquario Neo Flow lily pipes and media, it self-primes, and the baskets lift out separately for cleaning.
highlights: Rated for tanks up to about 61 L, 102 L, 250 L and 348 L
Low power draw: 7 W to 24 W
Aquario Neo Flow inflow and outflow pipes included (V2)
Neo Flow add-ons (skimmer, CO2 mixer, gentle outlet) fit straight on
bestFor: Nano to mid-size planted tanks where you want a small, tidy canister with clear lily pipes out of the box.

specs.Included: Aquario Neo Flow lily pipes, filter media (V2)

watchOut: Real flow at working height is roughly half the headline figure, so size up if you run CO2 in a densely planted tank.

name: Aqua Gravel
summary: A natural mixed-colour gravel in browns, greys and tans. It works for streambed details, filling gaps around stones or as a coarser foreground accent.
highlights: Natural rounded gravel in mixed earthy colours
Useful for streambeds and detailing around rock
bestFor: Adding texture and a natural riverbed look to the foreground of a planted tank.

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse before use

watchOut: Too coarse for carpet plants to root in, so use it as an accent rather than a planting substrate.

name: Colorado Sand
summary: A natural sand with a light sandy-beige tone, a touch warmer than La Plata Sand. It suits paths and foregrounds where you want a more natural, riverbed feel.
highlights: Good for paths, beaches and open foreground areas
bestFor: Nature-style and riverbank layouts that want a softer, warmer foreground than white sand.

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse before use

watchOut: Like any cosmetic sand, it will mix into soil unless the two are kept apart.

name: La Plata Sand
summary: A fine, pale natural sand used for paths, foreground patches and beach areas in nature aquariums. Its light colour brightens the front of a layout and contrasts well with dark aqua soil.
highlights: Classic choice for sand paths and open foreground areas
bestFor: Iwagumi and nature aquarium layouts that need a clean, bright foreground or path.

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse before use

watchOut: Keep it separated from soil with stones or a divider, or the two will mix over time.

name: Accent Driftwood
summary: Assorted small-to-large natural driftwood pieces sold in packs. They are meant for finishing touches: stacking at the base of a hardscape, wrapping with moss, or holding a few epiphytes.
highlights: Four size bands from about 5 cm to 64 cm+
Useful for layering and finishing details
bestFor: Filling gaps and adding detail around an existing hardscape rather than as a main piece.

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: May float at first
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

watchOut: Assorted wood types, so pieces will not always match each other.

name: Amazon Wood
summary: Mid-sized driftwood with knots, grooves and varied branching that combines the textures of several popular woods. Pieces fit together easily into larger wood layouts.
highlights: S, M and L sizes, about 20-51 cm
Knots and grooves for moss and rhizomes
bestFor: Tanks of about 40 litres and up that need several matching pieces for a larger wood build.

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Not stated; soak before use
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Ancient Stone
summary: A grey and brown stone in the same family of looks as Manten and Yama stone. Its angular, weathered shapes suit Iwagumi and it also makes a solid base under wood.
bestFor: Iwagumi keepers who like the Manten look and want a slightly darker, more angular stone.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Ashen Stone
summary: A pale, almost white stone with a smooth surface and rounded shapes. It gives a clean, minimal look and suits river layouts and bare-bottom tanks.
highlights: Smooth and rounded, no sharp edges
Good for goldfish and other delicate-finned fish
bestFor: Minimal or river-style scapes that want bright, soft stone against lush green planting.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Pale stone shows algae and diatoms quickly, and white stones are often limestone, so test it.

name: Basin Driftwood
summary: An ornamental driftwood with deep grooves, dips and bowl-like hollows. Those basins are perfect for tucking in Anubias, Buce or clumps of Java Fern.
highlights: S, M and L sizes, about 25-51 cm+ long
bestFor: Focal-point wood in nature layouts heavy on epiphytes.

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Usually sinks on its own in about two weeks
specs.Prep: Boil or soak to speed waterlogging

watchOut: Priced higher than most woods in the range.

name: Black Forest Spider Wood
summary: A dark, charcoal-brown spider wood that keeps getting darker over time, unlike normal spider wood which starts pale. It releases little tannin and has the same twisting, root-like branches.
highlights: Nano, S and M sizes from about 3 cm to 41 cm
Twisting root-like branches for moss and epiphytes
bestFor: Moody, dark scapes where you want branchy wood that contrasts with bright plants.

specs.Effect on water: Releases only a little tannin
specs.Buoyancy: Floats at first; soak or weigh down
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Black Lava Rock
summary: Classic porous black lava rock, sold in a 15 to 16 lb lot. It is light, so you get a lot of volume per kilo, and the rough surface is one of the easiest for moss and epiphytes to grab.
highlights: Excellent for moss, Anubias, Bucephalandra and ferns
Easy to break into smaller pieces
bestFor: Budget-friendly builds, nano tanks and moss-covered scapes that need plenty of stone volume.

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Rough edges can catch long fins, and it holds debris, so rinse it thoroughly first.

name: Black Lava Rock Cave
summary: Single pieces of black lava rock with one or more natural holes through them. Turn the opening forward for a shrimp or fish cave, or upward and fill it with soil for a little planted pocket.
highlights: Four sizes from about 15 cm to 30 cm across
Porous lava gives grip for stacking and for moss
Handy for nano tanks and small caves for shy fish and shrimp
bestFor: Shrimp and nano tanks that need hiding spots, or scapers wanting planted pockets at different heights.

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Rough surface can snag long fins, and hole size and position vary between pieces.

name: Black Mountain Seiryu Stone
summary: A near-black Seiryu variety with blue undertones and the same grooves and jagged forms as the classic grey stone. The dark colour makes bright green and red plants stand out.
highlights: Charcoal to almost black with a blue tinge
bestFor: Iwagumi and nature layouts where you want Seiryu shapes in a darker, moodier colour.

specs.Effect on water: Raises KH, GH and pH (calcareous, like all Seiryu-type stone)
specs.Colour: Charcoal to near black, blue undertone
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Raises hardness like normal Seiryu, so skip it for Caridina or soft-water fish.

name: Black Ridge Stone
summary: A layered, jagged stone in dark charcoal and earthy brown, with tiny reflective flecks that catch the light. The irregular ledges stack well into slopes and cliff faces.
highlights: 30 lb (about 13.6 kg) box of varied sizes
Charcoal and brown tones with a subtle glint under LEDs
Rugged, layered edges for slopes and terraces
Good ledges for moss and rhizome plants
bestFor: Layered mountain or tide-pool style scapes where you want to build height with stacked ledges.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Colour: Dark charcoal and earthy brown with fine flecks
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well; the seller advises against boiling

name: Black River Slate
summary: Flat dark grey slate that looks almost black underwater. Good for cave stacks, paths and moss stones, or as a base under intricate wood work.
highlights: Dark grey to near black when wet
Flat pieces for stacking and paths
Easy to split for moss wrapping
bestFor: Dark-toned layouts and cave stacks where you want slate that disappears into shadow.

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Colour: Dark grey, near black when wet
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Black Slate
summary: Black and grey slate with small white striations. The flat profile makes it easy to stack into caves and terraces, and it splits readily for paths and moss-wrapped accents.
bestFor: Cave builds, terraces and moss stones in any size of tank.

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Colour: Black and grey with fine white streaks
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Black Star Lava Rock
summary: Rounded, pebble-like lava rock that is much smoother than regular lava while keeping its porous surface. You still get lots of volume per kilo and a good home for moss and bacteria.
highlights: Porous surface for moss and epiphytes
bestFor: Tanks with bettas or fancy goldfish, or anyone who wants lava's benefits without sharp edges.

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Blue Mountain Seiryu Stone
summary: A darker, medium-grey Seiryu with a blue tinge and pale veins running through it. It gives more contrast than classic Seiryu while keeping the same sharp, grooved character.
highlights: Medium-dark grey with blue tinge and light veins
Well priced for a Seiryu variety
bestFor: Iwagumi scapes in hard or moderately hard water that want Seiryu shapes with a cooler colour.

specs.Effect on water: Raises KH, GH and pH (calcareous, like all Seiryu-type stone)
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Hardens water like other Seiryu, which matters for soft-water shrimp.

Sizes run from palm-sized nano trees to a 1.2 m long display piece
Fine twig canopy ready for moss or Riccia
Many designs sit on a heavy base that helps them stay put

Useful for building borders and retaining edges

summary: A dark charcoal stone with rounded knobs and pockets, a bit like a denser take on volcanic rock. The gaps and crevices are handy for wedging in Bucephalandra, Anubias and moss.

Deep charcoal and grey colour that makes greens pop
Knobbly, craggy shapes with natural planting gaps

name: Cholla Driftwood Tree
summary: Branching cholla cactus skeleton with a hollow core and holes all over. It grows biofilm that shrimp and snails graze, gives fry places to hide, and slowly softens the water.
highlights: S and M sizes, about 25-61 cm
Hollow and holey, great shrimp cover
bestFor: Shrimp tanks and fry-rearing setups where grazing surface and hiding spots matter more than looks.

specs.Buoyancy: Floats until waterlogged

name: Cloud Stone
summary: A soft grey and brown stone with white flecks and a weathered, eroded surface. It reads as mountains and cliffs without the heavy contrast of darker rock, so it suits scapes where the plants should do the talking.

Muted grey-brown colour with random white markings
Craggy, eroded texture that stacks into peaks
Works well with carpets, grasses and sandy paths
bestFor: Iwagumi and mountain-style layouts in 60 cm tanks and up, where you want enough stone for a full main-stone arrangement in one order.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Colour: Soft grey and brown with white markings
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well; the seller advises against boiling

watchOut: Only sold in a 30 lb lot, which is a lot of rock for a nano tank.

name: Cueva Stone
summary: A grey stone streaked with white and cream, with flecks of brown. It looks close to Ryuoh and Seiryu, with the same jagged texture that suits dynamic rockscapes.
bestFor: Iwagumi and rock-led layouts for keepers who want a Seiryu look with more white contrast.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated; Seiryu-like stones often raise KH and pH, so test before use
specs.Colour: Grey with white-cream striations and brown specks
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Dark Blue Slate Stone
summary: Flat blue-charcoal slate that turns much darker once wet. It stacks cleanly into caves and ledges and makes a stable base under driftwood.
highlights: Flat profile for stacking and caves
Easy to split into smaller pieces for moss stones
bestFor: Stacked cave and ledge builds, and as a stable, hidden base for wood layouts.

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Desert Stone
summary: A golden-orange stone with scattered craters that looks a lot like Dragon (Ohko) stone. It is tougher and less crumbly than Ohko, so it throws off less dust, and the rough texture holds epiphytes well.
highlights: Golden orange colour, similar to Ohko
Less fragile and dusty than Dragon stone
Lava-like texture for moss and Bucephalandra
bestFor: Anyone who likes the Dragon stone look but wants a sturdier, cleaner-to-handle rock.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Dragon Wood
summary: A driftwood with Malaysian-style colour and a pitted, holey surface like Dragon stone. Rhizome plants can often be pushed straight into the openings, no glue or thread needed.
highlights: Five sizes from about 8 cm to 61 cm+
Natural holes and cavities for planting
bestFor: Scapes heavy on Bucephalandra, Anubias, Java Fern and moss that should look mature quickly.

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Not stated; soak before use
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Elephant Skin Stone
summary: Also called Seegebirge, Elephant Skin is a light grey stone with a wrinkled, leathery surface from years of erosion. It is rounded rather than sharp, which gives a softer look than Seiryu.
highlights: Light grey with deep wrinkles and grooves
Good for bettas and fancy goldfish
bestFor: Iwagumi or nature layouts that want strong texture with soft edges, especially with delicate-finned fish.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated; some batches nudge hardness up slightly, so test before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Relatively expensive in the 20 and 30 lb lots.

name: Fire Stone
summary: A warm brown stone with a serrated, grippy texture full of crevices. It stacks well and suits caves, canyons and mountain terrain.
highlights: Serrated texture with lots of grip
Plenty of crevices for moss and plants
bestFor: Cave and canyon builds that need stones which lock together when stacked.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Flat Bottom Dragon Ohko Stone
summary: Ohko (Dragon) stone formations with a cut flat base so they stand straight up without propping. Drop one in for an instant rock scape, or combine several for a bigger tank.

Flat base, no need to wedge or glue
Classic Ohko scale texture and golden-brown colour
Tall enough to break the surface in small tanks

name: Flat Bottom Seiryu Stone

Flat-cut base for easy, stable placement
Classic grey Seiryu grooves and peaks
Can poke above the waterline in small tanks
bestFor: Small cube Iwagumi builds where you want a stable peak without fiddling (S suits 25 cm cubes, M suits 30 cm cubes).

specs.Effect on water: Raises KH, GH and pH (calcareous, like all Seiryu-type stone)
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

Rounded forms, kind to delicate fins
Good base under Malaysian or Spider Wood
bestFor: Nature layouts with carpets or sand where you want chunky stones that moss can colonise.

Very durable and slow to break down

bestFor: Beginners and nature-style scapers in any tank size, from nano Bucephalandra gardens to large layouts.

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Waterlogs faster than most; may need a brief soak
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Patagonia Stone
summary: A soft brown stone full of pores and holes, similar in texture to lava rock. The pitted surface is ideal for moss and epiphytes to grip onto.
highlights: Very porous with pockets and crevices
Stacks easily and works as a base for wood
bestFor: Low-tech and nature-style tanks where you plan to cover the stone with moss, Anubias or Bucephalandra.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated; light porous rock like this is usually inert, but test before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Petrified Wood Stone
summary: Fossilised wood that has turned to stone, so it looks like layered timber but behaves like rock. The banded brown, tan and grey tones work well alongside real driftwood.
bestFor: Nature-style scapes that want a stone which ties visually into the wood.

specs.Effect on water: Generally inert (silica based)
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Very heavy for its size, so protect the glass when placing big pieces.

name: Red Manten Stone
summary: A red-brown take on Manten, with orange, cream and beige showing in its weathered cracks. The warm colour contrasts strongly with green plants and looks at home in canyon and hillside scapes.
highlights: Deep reddish brown with orange and cream markings
Useful as a support stone under driftwood
bestFor: Warm-toned canyon or rocky hillside layouts, or anyone wanting a change from grey stone.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Colour: Reddish brown with orange, cream and beige
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well; the seller advises against boiling

name: Ryuoh Stone
summary: Sometimes sold as boutique Seiryu, Ryuoh is a charcoal grey stone with white marbling, deep grooves and jagged edges. It is medium weight: lighter than Hakkai, denser than lava.
highlights: Clean lines and sharp grooves for Iwagumi
Solid base for driftwood in nature layouts
bestFor: Iwagumi layouts where you want a darker, more dramatic alternative to standard Seiryu.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated; Seiryu-like stones usually raise KH and pH, so test before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Expect it to behave like Seiryu and harden the water unless your own test says otherwise.

name: Sand Stone
summary: A warm beige and cream stone with horizontal layered striations, like a weathered cliff face. It stacks easily and gives a softer, warmer palette than grey rock.
highlights: Layered striations for cliff and ridge looks
Mix of flat and taller angular pieces
bestFor: Warm-toned cliff, clearing or beach-style layouts, especially paired with driftwood.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Sandstone can be bound with calcium carbonate, so test it if you keep soft-water species.

name: Sandblasted Manzanita Driftwood
summary: Very branchy manzanita that has been sandblasted to a smooth, even pale finish. It builds tree and forest scenes easily and looks good bare or covered in moss.
highlights: Five sizes from about 15 cm to over 90 cm
bestFor: Tree-style and forest layouts, from small cubes up to large display tanks.

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Colour: Pale tan, turns browner once wet
specs.Buoyancy: Floats at first; soak before use
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

watchOut: Thin branches snap easily in transit and when scaping.

name: Seiryu Base Stone
summary: A 20 lb selection of long, flat, slab-like Seiryu pieces meant for building structure rather than as feature stones. Use them as retaining walls, supports under main stones and wood, or to shape slopes.
highlights: Same grey colour and texture as standard Seiryu
Good for terraces, retaining walls and substrate transitions
bestFor: Sloped or terraced Iwagumi and nature layouts that need hidden structure beneath the show stones.

specs.Effect on water: Raises KH, GH and pH (calcareous, like all Seiryu-type stone)
specs.Colour: Classic Seiryu grey with white veining
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Not meant as main stones, and like all Seiryu it pushes up hardness, so it is a poor fit for soft-water shrimp.

name: Seiryu Stone
summary: The classic Iwagumi stone: blue-grey with white veins, sharp ridges and deep grooves. It comes in every size from nano pebbles to big main stones and works just as well at the foot of driftwood.
highlights: 5, 10, 20 and 30 lb lots plus a 3 lb bag of small accent pieces
Jagged, grooved shapes with lots of character
Suits tanks from 4 litre cubes to large standards
bestFor: Iwagumi and nature layouts in tanks where a little extra hardness is fine, such as most community fish and Neocaridina setups.

specs.Effect on water: Raises KH, GH and pH (calcareous, like all Seiryu-type stone)
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use
