watchOut: Raises KH and pH over time, so it is a poor choice for Caridina shrimp or soft-water specialists.

name: Spider Wood
summary: The go-to branchy wood: a tangle of twisting, root-like branches with endless places to tie moss and epiphytes. It starts pale and darkens once waterlogged, and the Nano pieces add root detail in small tanks.
highlights: Sizes from about 8 cm (Nano) to 61 cm+ (XL)
Ideal for bonsai-style and forest scapes
bestFor: Forest, root and bonsai-inspired layouts in any tank size, often perched on Dragon stone or Seiryu.

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Colour: Pale tan, darkens to brown when wet
specs.Buoyancy: Floats until waterlogged; weigh down or soak
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

watchOut: Expect a week or two of floating and a harmless white fungal film early on.

name: Spider Wood on Slate Stone
summary: Spider wood already fixed to a flat slate base, so it goes straight into the tank without floating. Bury the slate under soil or let it show and add stones around it.
highlights: Five sizes from about 18 cm to 71 cm
Pre-attached slate base keeps the wood down
bestFor: Beginners and quick setups that want branchy wood without the floating problem.

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Colour: Light brown wood on grey slate
specs.Buoyancy: Held down by slate base
specs.Prep: Rinse; ready to use

watchOut: Branch shape is fixed to the base, so you have less freedom to angle the wood.

name: Star Wood
summary: Long, fairly straight branches with pointed tips, somewhere between Manzanita and Spider Wood. The predictable shape makes it easier to build clean triangular or central compositions.
highlights: Three sizes from about 41 cm to 71 cm+
Takes rhizome plants and moss well
bestFor: Wood-focused nature layouts in standard and larger tanks that need structured, directional lines.

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Floats at first; weigh down or soak
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

watchOut: Expect harmless white biofilm for the first few weeks.

name: Strata Pro Hardscape
summary: Ready-made layouts of real Dragon stone, with or without bonsai driftwood, fixed to a resin mat and sized for 36, 45 and 60 cm rimless tanks. You see exactly what you get, drop it in, add soil and plants, and the hardscape is done.
highlights: 17 designs built from natural Dragon stone, many with bonsai driftwood
Sized for 36 cm (Pro 5), 45 cm (Pro 45) and 60 cm (Pro 60) tanks
Everything is fixed to a resin base mat
Suggested planting: Anubias, Bucephalandra, Cryptocoryne and moss
bestFor: Beginners or busy keepers with a 36, 45 or 60 cm tank who want a finished, balanced hardscape without choosing and gluing stones.

specs.Effect on water: Dragon stone is inert; designs with wood release some tannins
specs.Colour: Golden-brown Dragon stone, brown bonsai wood
specs.Pro 5 size: about 28 x 18 x 20 cm, for 36 cm tanks
specs.Pro 45 size: about 38 x 23 x 25 cm, for 45 cm tanks
specs.Pro 60 size: about 58 x 28 x 30 cm, for 60 cm tanks
specs.Prep: Rinse before placing

watchOut: Expensive compared with buying loose stone and wood, and the layout is fixed, so there is no rearranging later.

name: Strata Seiryu Hardscape
summary: One-piece Iwagumi rock formations cast in lightweight aquarium-safe resin to look like Seiryu stone. Type 1 is taller and more dramatic, Type 2 is lower and more open to leave room for a carpet.
highlights: Seiryu look without the hardness increase
Sized for UNS 5N and 45U tanks; both together suit a 60U
Safe for fish, shrimp and plants
bestFor: First Iwagumi builds in 20-40 litre tanks, and soft-water shrimp keepers who love the Seiryu look but not its effect on KH.

specs.Effect on water: None (resin)

watchOut: It is resin, not real stone, and up close it will not have the variation of natural rock.

name: Striped River Stone
summary: Smooth, rounded river stones with striped patterns in white, grey, brown and orange. They look natural in river layouts and are safe around delicate fins.
highlights: Pairs well with sand and simple planting
bestFor: River-style scapes and tanks with fancy goldfish or bettas.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Colour: White, grey, brown and orange stripes
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Thorn Wood
summary: Straight sticks covered in short side spikes. Underwater the spikes read as tiny horizontal branches, which is great for creating depth in forest scapes, especially with moss tied on.
highlights: Straight stems with thorn-like side spurs
Takes moss well for underwater forests
bestFor: Forest-style layouts built from many vertical stems.

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water (quite strongly)
specs.Buoyancy: Floats; soak, boil or weigh down
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Tree Branch Driftwood
summary: Very branchy pieces with clusters of fine twigs, made for cascading tree and forest looks. Tie moss onto the twigs for an underwater canopy.
highlights: Nano, Medium and Large sizes, about 10-46 cm
Good anchor for moss and small epiphytes
Seller sizes it to tank volume
bestFor: Underwater tree scapes in nano to standard tanks (Nano for about 15-40 L, Medium for 40-75 L, Large for 75 L+).

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Floats at first; soak or weigh down
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Tree Root Driftwood
summary: Pale, forked root pieces that mimic the root system of a tree, in a standard and a more tangled version. Both suit tied-on moss or ferns wedged into the forks.
highlights: Tangled version with denser, gnarled roots
Sinks on its own in about two weeks
bestFor: Root-style details and small tree scenes in nano to mid-sized tanks.

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Usually sinks by itself within about two weeks
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

watchOut: Some sharp tips, so soften them with moss if you keep bettas.

name: Verdant Stone
summary: A muted grey-blue stone with grey-cream veins and the odd rust speck. It has a texture much like Seiryu, which holds moss well.
highlights: Works as a driftwood base or in Iwagumi
bestFor: Scapers wanting a cooler blue-grey stone for Iwagumi or as a base under wood.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Colour: Grey-blue with grey-cream veins and rust specks
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: White Elephant Skin Stone
summary: A cream and beige version of Elephant Skin, with the same wrinkled, grooved surface and soft edges. The light colour stands out against dark soil and green carpets.
highlights: Cream and beige rather than grey
Smooth edges, safe for bettas and goldfish
bestFor: Bright, high-contrast scapes over dark soil or carpets, and tanks with delicate-finned fish.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Light stone shows algae easily and is pricey in the larger lots.

name: Wolf Stone
summary: Something of a cross between Elephant Skin and Icelandic lava: grey, sharper and more jagged than Elephant Skin, and fairly porous. Moss and epiphytes attach readily.
highlights: Good for an aged, moss-covered look
bestFor: Nature layouts where the stone will carry mosses like Christmas, Pellia or Fissidens.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated; light porous rock like this is usually inert, but test before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Yukon Canyon Stone
summary: An earthy stone that ranges from grey to golden brown and beige. Its semi-flat, rounded pieces stack stably and blend into biotope and nature layouts.
highlights: Mixed grey, golden brown and beige tones
Semi-flat, rounded pieces that stack well
bestFor: Biotope and nature-style tanks that want a neutral, earthy base stone under wood.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: DR Digital Heater
summary: A newer glass heater with a small LED readout of the water temperature built into the tube, plus dry-run and overheat protection. Six sizes from 50 to 300 W.
bestFor: Everyday tropical tanks where you want to see the temperature without a separate thermometer.
watchOut: Glass heaters sit inside the tank, so plan a spot with good flow and hide it behind hardscape.

name: DR-9 Series Heater
summary: The older DR heater range, a glass tube with a built-in controller and LED display, plus dry-run and overheat protection. Seven sizes from 50 to 300 W.
bestFor: General tropical tanks on a budget.

name: GR Glass Heater
summary: A glass heater with a separate controller box showing the temperature on an LED display. Same concept as the titanium TR, in a cheaper glass tube.
bestFor: Medium tanks where you want an easy-to-read set point on the outside of the tank.

name: HT Adjustable Heater
summary: A basic adjustable glass heater with a dial on top and a printed thermometer strip on the tube. Six sizes from 50 to 300 W.
highlights: Printed temperature scale on the tube
bestFor: Budget heating for community and planted tanks.
watchOut: Dial-type heaters drift; check with a separate thermometer.

name: PTC Digital Heater
summary: A plastic-shelled PTC heater with an external controller, digital display and several probes. PTC elements heat quickly and run cooler on the surface than a glass element. High-wattage models for big tanks.
highlights: PTC element in an industrial plastic shell
bestFor: Large aquariums that need serious heating with accurate control.
watchOut: Overkill for most home planted tanks; the smallest model is 300 W.

name: TR Titanium Heater
summary: A thin titanium tube heater run from an external controller with an LED temperature readout. Titanium will not shatter, which is reassuring with large fish or in a sump.
bestFor: Sumps, large tanks or tanks with boisterous fish where a glass heater could crack.

name: Heater Pro
summary: An app-controlled inline heater that sits on your canister filter's outflow hose, so there is no glass tube in the tank. It shifts between high and low power to hold temperature and has overheat, dry-run and water-level cut-outs.
highlights: Inline on the filter hose, nothing inside the tank
Two hose sizes: 12/16 mm and 16/22 mm
Overheat, dry-run and auto shut-off protection
Suits tanks from about 38 to 435 L
bestFor: Rimless and show tanks with a canister filter where you want clean glass and precise, app-set temperature.
watchOut: The listed unit is 110 to 120 V, so check you get the right voltage version for your region.

name: AH-1000 Plastic Mini Heater
summary: A fully submersible plastic-cased mini heater preset to 25 °C, in 10 and 25 W sizes.
bestFor: A nano or small shrimp tank that just needs taking off the chill.
watchOut: No adjustment, so it will not suit fish that want cooler or warmer water; unplug before lifting it out.

name: AH-1006 Glass Heater
summary: A glass thermostat heater with a printed temperature scale and a perforated lower sleeve, in the same 25 to 500 W steps as the AH-1008.
highlights: Printed temperature scale on the tube
bestFor: A tropical tank where you want a cheap heater with a visible scale.
watchOut: Treat the scale as a guide and confirm with a separate thermometer.

name: AH-1008 Glass Heater
summary: A standard glass thermostat heater from 25 to 500 W, rated at roughly one watt per litre.
bestFor: A budget heater for a tropical planted tank, sized to your volume.
watchOut: Budget glass heaters can drift, so keep a thermometer in the tank and never run it out of water.

name: AH-1010 Mini Heater
summary: A tiny quartz heater with a switch for 23, 25 or 27 °C. The three wattages each suit a nano of 5, 10 or 15 litres.
bestFor: A small shrimp or betta tank where you just want a stable, sensible temperature.
watchOut: No fine control between the three settings, so check with a thermometer.

name: ThermoControl
summary: ThermoControl is Eheim's standard adjustable glass heater, and it is the one many keepers have running for years without a second thought. You set it between 20 and 32 °C on the dial, and the electronics hold it within about half a degree.
highlights: Red and green lamp shows when it is heating
Dry-run protection switches it off if the water drops
bestFor: Almost any planted tank, from nano to very large, where you want a proven heater you can set and forget.
watchOut: It is glass with no guard, so keep it clear of big digging fish and never lift it out while it is hot.

name: thermocontrol+e
summary: The thermocontrol+e is a glass heater with WiFi built in. You set the temperature from a browser, and it e-mails you if the water drifts more than 2 °C from target. It can also link to Eheim filters and lights to run a slightly cooler night.
highlights: Set 18 to 32 °C from a phone, tablet or computer
E-mail alert if temperature drifts by ±2 °C
Expert mode lets you calibrate against your own thermometer
Day and night temperature via Eheim's digital family
bestFor: Larger tanks where you want remote alerts about temperature, especially if you are away a lot.
watchOut: Smallest size is 150 W for 200 litres and up, and it must be mounted upright, which can be awkward in some sumps.

name: ThermoPreset
summary: ThermoPreset is fixed at 25 °C with nothing to adjust. It is slim, around 2.8 cm across, and wrapped in a plastic sleeve, so it is a sensible pick for a simple community tank or a first aquarium.
highlights: Factory set to 25 °C, no dial to knock
Plastic casing, tougher than a bare glass tube
Dry-run protection and an LED heating lamp
bestFor: Beginners and community planted tanks that are happy at 25 °C.
watchOut: You cannot change the temperature, so it is no good for cooler-water species or shrimp that prefer low 20s.

name: AquaHeat
summary: Juwel's adjustable glass heaters, made in borosilicate glass with TÜV/GS safety certification. They are shaped to sit inside the Bioflow filter housing in Juwel aquariums, where they stay out of sight and heat the water as it passes through. They work in any tank, but they make most sense in a Juwel.
highlights: 50 W AquaHeat and 100, 200, 300 W AquaHeat Pro
Fits inside Juwel Bioflow filter housings
bestFor: Juwel aquarium owners replacing or upgrading the heater inside their Bioflow filter.

specs.Fits: Juwel Bioflow filter housings, or any tank

name: HeatUp
summary: An adjustable glass heater with a bimetal thermostat, available from 25 W to 400 W. It is the same heater Oase builds into its Thermo filters, and it can be fitted into a FiltoSmart or BioMaster later, or used in the tank with the supplied holder. A plain, dependable choice if you just want a heater that holds temperature.
highlights: Retrofits into FiltoSmart and BioMaster filters
Mounting holder included for in-tank use
bestFor: Oase filter owners who want to add heating later, or anyone after a simple adjustable heater.
watchOut: A 25 to 50 W unit is still 20 cm long, so check it fits a shallow nano.

name: AR Series Aquarium Heater
summary: A broad range of adjustable heaters from 50 to 1,000 W: compact AR-2 units and flat AR-3 heaters for bigger tanks and sumps. Rated from 20 to 900 litres.
bestFor: Any size tank, including sumps that need a lot of heat.

name: ARB Digital Heater
summary: A high-power heater (500 to 1,000 W) with a separate digital display controller, remote and thermistor probe. Built for 300 to 900 litre tanks.
bestFor: Large display tanks and sumps.

name: JRB Aquarium Heater
summary: A classic adjustable glass heater in 100 to 500 W sizes, plus the YRB-065, a small preset heater fixed at 26 °C. Sized by tank length.
bestFor: Everyday tropical tanks.

name: XRB Intelligent Heater
summary: A 600 or 1,000 W heater with an external controller, from SunSun's Xiaoli line, for 300 to 900 litre tanks.
bestFor: Large tanks and sumps.

name: YRB-250 Remote Heater
summary: A 500 W heater with an external controller and remote control, for 100 to 120 cm tanks. The ARB-250 is the same heater in a different finish.
bestFor: Large tanks where you want to check and set temperature easily.

name: YRB-800 Electronic Heater
summary: An electronic heater with an external controller that holds temperature to about 1 °C and remembers its setting after a power cut. Also sold as the ZRB series.
bestFor: Mid to large tanks where you want to set and read temperature outside the water.

name: YRB-900 Aquarium Heater
summary: An adjustable heater range from a small 30 W up to 500 W, sized by tank length. It is short for its power (18 to 28 cm).
bestFor: Nano to large tanks.

name: ZTB Aquarium Heater
summary: An adjustable heater from SunSun's Zhizhen line, from 50 to 1,000 W, with a 20 to 35 °C range. SunSun rates each size by tank volume.
bestFor: Any freshwater tank, sized to its volume.

name: Micro Aquarium Heater
summary: A very small heater for pico and nano tanks, with the thermostat and display on an external controller on the cable. The heating element is tiny enough to hide behind a rock, and it switches itself off if the water drops too low.
highlights: 10 W for about 4 to 8 L, 20 W for about 8 to 19 L
External digital controller on the cable
10 W runs from USB; 20 W uses a mains plug
bestFor: Betta tanks and nano cubes under 20 litres where a normal glass heater would dominate the tank.

specs.Safety: Auto shut-off when water level is low

watchOut: The 20 W version has a US mains plug and 110 V rating, so check it suits your country's supply.

name: Aquasky RGB II
summary: ADA's slim RGB LED that stands on legs outside the glass of a 60 cm tank. It is controlled over Bluetooth from ADA's phone app, with colour, brightness and timer settings, and a soft fade on and off.
highlights: 70 RGB LEDs, up to 40,000 lux at 10 cm
Draws up to 66 W at full output
Legs rest outside the glass, so any glass thickness works on a 60 cm wide tank
Bluetooth app control with presets, colour tuning and a timer
Flicker-free, which helps when filming or photographing the tank
bestFor: A 60 cm planted tank where you want strong, tunable light and a clean ADA look without a separate controller.

specs.Colour temperature: About 8,000 to 11,000 K in default mode

watchOut: It is made for 60 cm tanks only, and full power is a lot of light for a low-tech tank without CO2.

name: CB Ultrathin LED
summary: A basic, very thin white LED bar with extendable brackets that rest on the tank rim. Five lengths from 50 to 140 cm.
bestFor: Low-tech planted and community tanks where you just need decent white light.
watchOut: No dimming, timer or published PAR, and wattage per length drops off on the longest bars.

name: CL Clamp Lamp
summary: Small clamp-on lamps with an adjustable aluminium head. The P models take PL compact fluorescent tubes, the L models use LEDs. Old-school but fine for a nano.
highlights: PL fluorescent (5 to 13 W) or LED (1.2 to 2.2 W)
bestFor: Nano and small tanks with low-light plants.
watchOut: The LED versions are very low wattage and will only grow the easiest plants.

name: CM-10 LED Clip Light
summary: A compact clip-on LED panel with touch control and several lighting modes. Runs on a low-voltage adaptor.
bestFor: Nano tanks and desktop scapes with easy plants.
watchOut: No spectrum or PAR data published.

name: ZN WiFi LED
summary: A slim aluminium LED bar with app control over timing, brightness and colour, including a 24-hour sunrise-to-sunset cycle. There is also an IR remote.
highlights: App control of timer, brightness and colour
bestFor: Planted tanks from 45 to 90 cm where you want scheduling and colour control on a budget.
watchOut: Boyu gives no PAR or lumen data, and lists the ZN-60 at the same length as the ZN-45, which looks like a sheet error.

name: ZN-800 / ZN-1600 Arm LED
summary: Fan-cooled LED spots on a gooseneck arm that clamps to the tank edge. The ZN-800 is a single puck, the ZN-1600 a twin-lens bar with app control. Knobs let you dim and shift the colour temperature.
bestFor: Open-top tanks where you want a hanging-style look without a ceiling mount.
watchOut: The colour dial runs between blue and white, which hints at a marine focus, and there is no PAR data.

name: A II Max
summary: A brighter, bigger sibling of the A II with nearly double the output per size and a wider size range up to 140 cm tanks. It ships on metal legs, and Chihiros sells acrylic legs and a hanging kit if you want a different look.
highlights: Six sizes covering 30 cm to 140 cm tanks
Up to 8,100 lm on the 1201 Max
Bluetooth app: brightness, timer and schedules
Metal legs as standard; hanging kit and acrylic legs available
bestFor: Medium-light planted tanks from nano to large that want a simple, bright, app-controlled bar at a fair price.

specs.Mounting: Metal rim legs (acrylic legs and hanging kit optional)

watchOut: The retailer pitches its spectrum at low-tech scapes, so it is less suited to showing off red plants than an RGB light.

name: A II Series
summary: A very slim Chihiros bar on clear acrylic clamp legs that can swivel, so you can angle the light toward one part of the scape. Output is moderate and the spectrum leans toward red and blue, with Bluetooth app control built in.
highlights: Four sizes for 30, 36, 45 and 60 cm tanks
8000 K full spectrum weighted to red and blue
bestFor: Nano and small low to medium light tanks where you want app control and a nearly invisible fixture.
watchOut: Clamps fit glass up to 8 mm only, and output is modest for carpets without CO2.

name: B Series
summary: Chihiros' straightforward WRGB bar: white LEDs with a few RGB diodes mixed in, adjustable legs and Bluetooth control. It is a no-fuss light for everyday planted tanks, available in seven lengths.
highlights: Seven sizes from 20 cm to 120 cm
White plus RGB LEDs for natural colour
Bluetooth app for brightness and timers
Adjustable legs; shade and hanging kit sold separately
bestFor: Low to medium demand planted tanks and beginners who want app scheduling without spending much.
watchOut: Models up to B60 only clamp glass up to 8 mm (12 mm for larger ones), and B80 specs weren't listed by the retailer.

name: C II Series
summary: A compact clamp-on light on a vertical pole, so you can set both height and angle over a nano tank. It comes in a white version or an RGB version.
highlights: White (1,500 lm) or RGB (1,580 lm) versions
Adjustable height and swivel on a pole clamp
Bluetooth app for brightness, schedule, sunrise/sunset and colour (RGB model)
Optional base for use away from a tank
bestFor: Small nano tanks and open-top bowls where one compact, adjustable light is enough.
watchOut: The clamp fits glass up to 8 mm only, and the display base is an extra purchase.

name: C Series
summary: A simple clip-on nano light that hangs over the tank on a short arm. It is inexpensive, easy to fit and bright enough for small planted tanks.
highlights: Four sizes for 20 to 36 cm tanks
Clip-on arm for rimless glass up to 6 mm
bestFor: Nano tanks from roughly 8 to 38 L with easy to moderate plants.
watchOut: Only fits glass up to 6 mm thick, and it has no app control.

name: Magnetic Light 2
summary: A palm-sized round puck light with a magnetic back, meant to stick to a metal stand or the included adhesive plate. It has a small cooling fan and mixes RGB and white LEDs, with control through the Chihiros app.
highlights: App control of brightness, colour channels and sunrise/sunset
Magnetic mounting with adhesive metal pad included
bestFor: Tiny tanks, or spotlighting a single plant or stone where a bar light won't fit.
watchOut: You need a metal stand or surface to mount it, and at around 800 lm it only lights a small footprint.

name: Nano Universal RGB
summary: A clip-on RGB nano light in two sizes, made for 20 to 36 cm tanks. It is fully waterproof to IP67 and has Bluetooth control, so it handles a humid open-top nano without complaint.
highlights: Nano 20 and Nano 30 sizes for 20 to 36 cm tanks
Bluetooth app: brightness, timer, spectrum and effects
Clips on glass up to 10 mm
bestFor: Shrimp tanks, betta tanks and small planted nanos that want colour control in a compact clip-on.
watchOut: Two sizes only, so anything past 36 cm needs a different light.

name: RGB Vivid II (10th Edition)
summary: The compact but very powerful RGB panel that made the Vivid name, here in its 10th Edition. It packs 130 W and over 12,000 lm into the same 35 cm body as the Vivid Mini. It is being phased out in favour of the Vivid Mini and Vivid 3.
highlights: App control of colour, brightness and sunrise/sunset
bestFor: Tall or demanding high-tech tanks where one small panel has to deliver a lot of light.
watchOut: Discontinued, and the stand or hanging kit shown in photos is sold separately.

name: RGB Vivid II Mate
summary: A pared-back version of the Vivid II with fewer LEDs, keeping the same shape, app and full RGB channel control. At 125 W it still has far more output than most 60 to 90 cm tanks need, and it comes with a hanging kit.
highlights: One fixture for 60 to 90 cm tanks
Individual RGB channel control in the MyChihiros app
bestFor: High-tech 60 to 90 cm tanks, especially deeper ones, where you want a pendant with lots of headroom.
watchOut: Expensive, and you will rarely run it near full power without inviting algae.

name: RGB Vivid Mini
summary: A compact 35 cm RGB panel with 75 W of output, sold either with a rim-mounted bar or as a pendant with a hanging kit. It brings Vivid-level colour and punch to smaller high-tech tanks.
highlights: RGB LEDs with full app control of colour and effects
Standard rim bar or pendant version
Optional WiFi hub for remote control
bestFor: Smaller high-tech tanks, or deeper nanos, where you want strong RGB colour from a compact panel.
watchOut: The shade is sold separately, and the pendant version comes without the rim-mount bar.

name: WRGB II Pro
summary: The high-output member of the WRGB II family, with a dedicated white channel on top of full RGB and a higher LED count. It is still slim, and gives strong light and colour for demanding scapes.
highlights: Six sizes from 30 cm to 120 cm
Up to 11,170 lm on the Pro 120
White plus RGB channels, each adjustable in the app
bestFor: High-tech planted tanks and deeper aquariums where you want lots of output and control over colour.
watchOut: More light than a low-tech tank can use; dim it right down if you don't run CO2.

name: WRGB II Slim
summary: A thinner, lower-output take on the WRGB II with full colour control in the app. At about 1.5 cm thick, it disappears over a rimless tank and suits most planted setups from low to fairly demanding.
highlights: Five sizes from 30 cm to 120 cm
WRGB with app control of colour and brightness
bestFor: Everyday planted tanks where you want RGB colour tuning and a very low-profile fixture.
watchOut: Roughly half the output of the WRGB II Pro, so it is less suited to deep high-tech tanks.

name: WRGB Vivid 3
summary: Chihiros' flagship planted-tank light, a wide flat panel only 23 mm thick with a snap-on magnetic fan. Output now goes up to 180 W and 16,600 lm, which is serious light for tall or large high-tech scapes.
highlights: WRGB with white plus RGB 3-in-1 LEDs
App control of brightness, colour, timing and fan
bestFor: Large or deep high-tech tanks with CO2 where you want maximum light and colour tuning from one fixture.
watchOut: Very expensive and very powerful; smaller or low-tech tanks will struggle to use it well.

name: Z Light Tiny
summary: A tiny spotlight on an articulated arm with a zoom lens, used to pick out a single plant, stone or focal point. The Diving Edition can even go underwater for shadow and uplighting effects.
highlights: Diving Edition is IP67 and submersible
bestFor: Adding highlights or accent lighting to a nano or display tank alongside a main light.
watchOut: It is an accent light, not a main light for growing plants; only the Diving Edition may be submerged.

name: LED 109 Clip Light
summary: A slim 3.4 W clip-on LED with 12 white and 3 blue diodes on an arched arm. It clamps to glass up to 5 mm thick.
bestFor: A small nano with low-light plants such as Anubias, Bucephalandra, Java fern and mosses.
watchOut: Too weak for carpeting plants or red stems; treat it as a viewing light that keeps easy plants ticking over.

name: Mini LED Clip Light
summary: Small clip-on lights for tiny tanks: a gooseneck 8-LED spot and flat 10, 14 and 20 LED panels on a swivel clamp.
bestFor: Lighting a desktop tank or betta setup with a few low-light plants.

specs.Mount: Clip-on (gooseneck on 8 LED, swivel clamp on the others)

watchOut: Wattage and spectrum are not published; expect only enough light for the hardiest plants.

name: powerRGB
summary: powerRGB is a low-voltage RGB LED bar meant to sit alongside your main light and add colour. On its own it gives a fixed output. Paired with the RGBcontrol+e controller (sold separately) you can blend colours, run sunrise and sunset, and add moonlight.
highlights: Adds red, green and blue to lift plant and fish colour
Three lengths for tanks from about 79 to 125 cm
bestFor: Tanks that already have a white main light and where you want richer reds and greens, or smooth dawn and dusk.
watchOut: It is a supplementary light, not a full planted-tank light on its own, and the colour control needs an extra controller.

name: HeliaLux Spectrum
summary: Juwel's step-up LED bar, with white LEDs at 9,000 K and 6,500 K plus red, green and blue channels. It drops into any Juwel tank with a fixed top frame, and a UniversalFit holder lets it sit on other tanks too. Compared with the stock MultiLux it adds colour channels and, with the SmartControl or AppControl added, dimming and scheduling.
highlights: Eight lengths from 55 to 150 cm to match Juwel tanks
White plus RGB LEDs for plant growth and better colour rendering
About 140 lumens per watt, with aluminium honeycomb heat sinks
Scratch-resistant safety glass over the LEDs
bestFor: Juwel tank owners who want to grow a wider range of plants than the stock MultiLux allows.

specs.LEDs: White 9,000 K and 6,500 K plus red, green and blue
specs.Mounting: Juwel tanks with fixed top frame; UniversalFit holder for other tanks

watchOut: Dimming, sunrise and colour control need the HeliaLux SmartControl or AppControl, sold separately.

name: MultiLux LED
summary: The standard light unit fitted to Juwel's LED aquariums, holding two replaceable glass LED tubes (one DAY, one NATURE). It is sealed against moisture and lets you work in the tank with the light on. Buying one on its own makes sense for replacing a T5 unit or a broken lid light.
highlights: Eight lengths from 55 to 150 cm to fit Juwel tanks
Two replaceable LED tubes, 9,000 K and 6,500 K
Moisture-blocking membrane keeps the unit dry
Roughly half the energy of the old T5 units
bestFor: Juwel owners converting from T5 or replacing a lid light for a low-light planted or community tank.

specs.Tubes: 2 x replaceable Juwel LED tubes (DAY and NATURE fitted)

watchOut: There is no dimming or scheduling built in, so plan on a plug-in timer, or look at the HeliaLux Spectrum if you want control.

name: HighLine Classic LED
summary: A slim, fully waterproof LED tube in a 6,500 K daylight tone, made as the lighting for Oase HighLine aquariums. Each tube has its own on/off switch and is IP68 rated, and it fits other tanks with compatible holders. HighLine tanks are usually lit with two of these side by side.
highlights: IP68 waterproof with inline toggle switch
Daylight spectrum suited to plants and natural colours
bestFor: HighLine owners, or anyone wanting simple, waterproof daylight tubes for a low to medium-light tank.
watchOut: No dimming or scheduling on its own; you will want a plug-in timer.

name: MotionControl LED
summary: Oase's controllable LED bar with four channels: neutral white, cool white, royal blue and red. Through the Oase aquarium controller and app you can set colour and intensity by segment and run sunrise and sunset effects. It is freshwater only and IP68 sealed, with a thin 15 mm profile.
highlights: Neutral white, cool white, royal blue and red LEDs
Segment-by-segment colour and brightness control via app
IP68 waterproof, no condensation inside the housing
bestFor: Keepers with an Oase HighLine or ScaperLine who want app-controlled, adjustable-spectrum lighting.

specs.Channels: Neutral white, cool white, royal blue, red
specs.Control: Oase aquarium controller and app (sold separately); IR control set optional
specs.Power supply: Oase Control Aquarium Transformer 120 W (sold separately)

watchOut: It needs the Oase aquarium controller and 120 W Control transformer, both sold separately, so the real cost is higher than the bar alone.

name: ADE LED Light
summary: A slim 63 mm wide LED bar for tanks from about 28 to 113 cm, with more output per length than the ADP. Six sizes from 12 to 28 W.
highlights: Six sizes for tanks 28 to 113 cm
bestFor: Low to medium light planted tanks on a budget.

specs.Mount: Adjustable legs on the tank rim

watchOut: Brightness does not scale much with length (28 W at 90 cm), so longer tanks get less light per litre.

name: ADF LED Light
summary: A wide 22.5 cm LED panel-bar for big tanks from 70 to 150 cm, from 45 to 90 W. The width spreads light across deeper tanks better than a narrow strip.
highlights: Four sizes for tanks 70 to 150 cm
bestFor: Larger planted tanks that need a bright, wide light.

specs.Mount: Adjustable legs on the tank rim

name: ADP Slim LED Light
summary: A very slim (7 mm) LED bar on adjustable legs, in 11 lengths from 8 cm up to 110 cm. It is the light SunSun pairs with its HEK and HWK open tanks.
bestFor: Low-tech planted tanks, shrimp tanks and fish-only setups that want a neat, low-profile light.

specs.Mount: Adjustable legs on the tank rim

watchOut: Output is low for the size (about 16 W on a 100 cm tank), so it is for easy, low-light plants only.

name: ADS LED Light
summary: A 10 cm wide LED bar for tanks from 38 to 130 cm, in fixed C7 aquatic versions and dimmable T versions. The larger C7 models reach 60 to 80 W.
highlights: C7 aquatic versions from 14 to 80 W
bestFor: Medium-light planted tanks where you want a single bar with decent output.

specs.Mount: Adjustable legs on the tank rim

watchOut: The H (sea light) versions in the same range are for marine tanks; pick C7 or T for plants.

name: ADT Round Clip Light
summary: A round 20 cm LED disc on a clamp arm, made in freshwater versions of 48 and 80 W. The 100C is the brighter 'glare' version for 60 to 80 cm tanks.
highlights: Clamps to glass up to 20 mm
bestFor: Mid-size open-top planted tanks where a single bright light is enough.
watchOut: SunSun also sells H (seawater) versions of this light; make sure you pick the C models for a planted tank.

name: ADT-2 Stand Light
summary: A cube-shaped LED spotlight on a rim-mounted arm, with vents on three sides for cooling. The 240C and 260C let you adjust brightness and colour temperature, covering tanks from 30 to 60 cm.
highlights: Two colour modes, adjustable on 240C and 260C
Clamps to glass 5 to 18 mm thick
bestFor: Small open-top planted tanks where you want a strong, focused light.
watchOut: A single spotlight suits roughly cube-shaped tanks better than long, shallow ones.

name: ADT-3 Stand Light
summary: A larger aluminium spotlight for 40 to 80 cm tanks, with adjustable power and colour temperature and two switchable modes. It hangs from a T3 rim-mounted stand.
bestFor: Medium open-top planted tanks that need more punch than a nano light.
watchOut: Spotlights can leave the corners of a rectangular tank darker than the centre.

name: ADT-880C Panel Light
summary: A flat 58 × 30 cm LED panel held over the tank on two stand brackets, rated for tanks up to 120 cm. Power and colour temperature are adjustable up to 80 W.
bestFor: Open-top planted tanks where you want a wide, even spread from one fixture.
watchOut: At 58 cm long, a 120 cm tank will have darker ends; it works best on tanks near its own length.

name: ADT-I Nano Stand Light
summary: A small cylindrical LED spotlight hung from an arm that clamps to the tank rim, sized for nano and small tanks from 20 to 60 cm. SunSun ships it with several of its tanks, and it gives an open-top tank a clean, gallery look.
highlights: Clamps to glass 5 to 18 mm thick
bestFor: Nano planted tanks and small shrimp setups with an open top.

specs.Mount: Clamp-on stand arm (T1 or T2 bracket)

watchOut: One puck light gives a pool of light rather than even coverage, so the edges of a wider tank stay dimmer.

name: ADZ Metal LED Spotlight
summary: A small metal-bodied mains LED spotlight (4.5 cm across) in 3, 5 and 7 W, with warm or three-colour adjustable white. It works as an accent light over an open nano tank.
bestFor: Accent lighting on a small open-top nano, or picking out a focal stone or plant alongside a main light.
watchOut: SunSun gives no mounting details or tank sizing, so plan how you will hang or aim it.

name: AMD Hang-On Nano Light
summary: A tiny USB-powered (5 V) LED that hooks over thin glass, for nano tanks up to about 50 cm. The AD-150 is a small clip-on lamp for tanks under 30 cm.
bestFor: Betta tanks, pico scapes and shrimp cubes with easy plants.
watchOut: Only fits thin glass (5 mm or less) and is a low-light option.

name: Dream White Plant Tube Light
summary: A sealed tube light from SunSun's Dream range, in the white version made for aquatic plants. It comes in six lengths for tanks from 80 cm to 2 m.
bestFor: Large tanks that already have a lid and want a simple plant-oriented tube.
watchOut: Output is low for the tank sizes it targets (30 W for 2 m), so treat it as a supplement or for undemanding plants.

name: ZDO Amphibious Tube Light
summary: A sealed LED tube that can run in or out of water, from SunSun's Zhizhen line, for tanks from 1.2 m upward. Four lengths from 98 to 170 cm.
bestFor: Big lidded fish tanks that want extra or replacement lighting.
watchOut: Low output for such long tanks; it will not drive a demanding planted setup on its own.

name: A Series
summary: Twinstar's entry-level light, a thin WRGB bar on an adjustable bracket so one unit can span a range of tank lengths. Output is modest, which makes it a fair match for fish-first tanks and easy plants rather than carpets.
highlights: Six sizes, each covering a range of tank lengths
Inline controller with 3 timer settings, 7 brightness levels and sunrise/sunset (version 2)
bestFor: Beginners and low-tech tanks with hardy plants where a simple timer and dimmer is all you need.
watchOut: Not bright enough for demanding stem plants or carpets; version 1 units shipped without the controller.

name: B Series Ver.3
summary: Twinstar's budget WRGB line, now in its third version with Bluetooth control included. It gives clean whites and decent colour for low to medium light planted tanks, and it is a sensible pick for a first scape or a second tank.
highlights: Seven sizes from 20 cm to 130 cm
WRGB LEDs for natural colour on plants and fish
LightControl Standard Bluetooth controller included (timer, dimming, sunrise/sunset, Light Planner)
Low power draw, 10 W on the smallest to 52 W on the 120B
bestFor: Low-tech tanks with Anubias, ferns, mosses, Cryptocorynes and easy stems, or anyone after an affordable app-controlled light.

specs.Control: Bluetooth app (LightControl Standard included, no colour channel control)

watchOut: Twinstar itself says one 75B, 90B or 120B may be too weak for a planted tank of that length, and suggests running two.

name: C Series
summary: A lightweight RGB-W bar with telescopic legs that stretch up to about 15 cm, so one fixture can cover several tank lengths. Brightness is set with buttons on the light itself across 15 steps. The line has been discontinued, so you will mostly find it second hand or as remaining stock.
highlights: Fits rimless glass up to 12 mm
bestFor: Low to medium light tanks where you want flexible fitting across tank sizes and don't need an app.
watchOut: Discontinued, and there is no built-in timer mentioned, so plan on a plug timer.

name: E Series Ver.5
summary: Twinstar's mid-power line, sitting under the S Series in output but using the same fifth-generation LED mix of six colour channels plus dedicated plant-growth diodes. It suits planted tanks with a mix of easy and moderately demanding plants, and it comes in seven sizes from a 20 cm nano up to a 120 cm show tank.
highlights: Seven sizes covering 20 cm to 130 cm tanks
RGB plus plant-growth LEDs for strong colour rendering, especially on red plants
Bluetooth app control with timer, 100-step dimming, sunrise/sunset and a 25-day ramp-up planner
Draws roughly 20% less power than the matching S Series model
Slim metal body on legs that rest on rimless glass
bestFor: Medium-light planted tanks where you want good colour and app scheduling without paying for the S Series' extra punch.

specs.Control: Bluetooth app (LightControl Pro with 4-channel colour, or LightControl Standard)

watchOut: Buy the LightControl Pro version if you want to adjust the colour channels; the Standard controller only does brightness and timing.

name: EA Series (E IV)
summary: The fourth-generation E line, also sold as E IV. It added orange LEDs to the RGB mix, which makes green plants look particularly rich, and has adjustable legs plus a built-in dimmer. It is an older model now, replaced by E Series Ver.5.
highlights: Six sizes from 20 cm to 120 cm
RGB plus orange LEDs at 8300 K
bestFor: Medium-light rimless tanks where you like the look of a very thin fixture and want a simple dimmer.
watchOut: No app or timer; superseded by the Ver.5 E Series with Bluetooth control.

name: S Series Ver.5
summary: The strongest Twinstar line, built for high-tech tanks with CO2 and light-hungry plants like carpets and red stems. Version 5 pairs six colour channels with plant-growth LEDs and phone control, and the 600S and larger can be hung from a wire kit instead of sitting on legs.
highlights: Six sizes for 20 cm to 130 cm tanks
Highest output in the Twinstar range, up to 7,600 lm on the 1200S
Bluetooth app with timer, 100-step dimming, boost mode and sunrise/sunset
600S and up can be suspended with the optional wire kit
bestFor: High-tech planted tanks running pressurised CO2 where you want plenty of headroom and fine control over colour.

specs.Spectrum: RGB + plant-growth LEDs (6 colour channels), 400 to 780 nm
specs.Control: Bluetooth app (LightControl Pro with 4-channel colour, or LightControl Standard)
specs.Dimming: 100 steps, sunrise/sunset up to 60 min, boost mode
specs.Mounting: Rim legs; wire hanging kit for 600S and larger

watchOut: There is enough output here to cause algae in a tank without CO2 and good fertilising, so start well below full power.

name: SA Series (S IV)
summary: The fourth-generation S Series, a high-output bar that can sit on the rim or hang as a pendant with Twinstar's wire kit. It has a manual dimmer rather than an app, and packs enough light for demanding plants.
highlights: Six sizes from 20 cm to 120 cm
Up to 6,750 lm on the 1200 model
Rim mount or pendant with the optional wire kit
bestFor: High-light planted tanks where you want strong output and are happy to schedule it with a plug timer.
watchOut: No app or built-in timer, and the wire kit for hanging is sold separately.

name: SM Series
summary: The original Twinstar S light (later labelled SM), a bright fixture on fixed metal legs. It predates app control, so it is simply on or off at full output.
highlights: Four sizes from 30 cm to 90 cm
Fixed metal legs for rimless tanks
Strong output for its era, up to 5,250 lm
bestFor: Rimless tanks matched to the exact light length where you run CO2 and use a plug timer.
watchOut: Legs don't adjust and there is no dimming mentioned, so it must match your tank length.

name: SP Series
summary: The suspended version of the older S Series, hung from above so the top of the tank stays open for maintenance. It has been discontinued but still turns up on larger display tanks.
highlights: Three sizes for 60, 90 and 120 cm tanks
Hangs above the tank for an open top
bestFor: Larger high-tech tanks where you want a pendant look and room to reach in.
watchOut: Discontinued, and you need a ceiling or bracket to hang it from.

name: Titan 1 RGB LED
summary: A 90 W hanging LED with 200 RGB diodes in a wide aluminium body. One unit covers a 60 to 90 cm tank, and the wide spread keeps the light even across the footprint rather than hot in the middle.
highlights: One unit covers a 60 to 90 cm tank; use two or more for bigger tanks
About 300 PAR directly under the light at 30 cm
Exposed heat-sink fins to shed heat
bestFor: Mid-size high-tech planted tanks where you want a pendant hung above an open-top rimless tank.

specs.Mounting: Suspension wires (97 cm) included; hanging kit sold separately

extra.Recommended hanging height: 30 cm or more above the tank

watchOut: It is designed to hang at least 30 cm above the water; the ceiling or hanging kit is sold separately.

name: Lily Pipe
summary: ADA's glass inflow and outflow pipes that replace the plastic pipes of a canister filter. The outflow's flared lip spreads water in a gentle wide stream, and the clear glass nearly vanishes in the tank.
highlights: Clear glass for a clean, almost invisible look
Outflow P-4 has a flared mouth for a soft, wide flow
Inflow V-5 has a slotted intake and suction cup mount
bestFor: Planted tanks with a canister filter where the plumbing is on show and you want it to disappear.
watchOut: Glass breaks easily and shows biofilm quickly, so it needs gentle handling and regular pipe-brush cleaning.

name: Metal Flow Pipe
summary: Stainless steel versions of ADA's inflow and outflow pipes. They keep the slim lily-pipe shape but will not snap if knocked, and the outflow nozzle swivels to aim the flow.
highlights: Stainless steel, far tougher than glass
Outflow P-1 has a rotating nozzle to direct flow
Inflow V-1 has a slotted intake and removable end cap
Brushed finish blends in better than shiny plastic
bestFor: Keepers who like the lily-pipe look but have broken glass pipes before, or have kids and pets around the tank.
watchOut: They are not see-through, so they are more visible than glass in a bright tank.

name: SK200 Surface Skimmer
summary: A small self-powered surface skimmer with its own 3 W pump. It pulls the oily film off the surface and returns the water, improving gas exchange.
bestFor: A small planted tank with a surface film problem that has no skimmer on the filter intake.
watchOut: At 200 L/h it is sized for small tanks, and the surface agitation it creates will drive off some CO2.

name: skim350
summary: The skim350 is a small powered surface skimmer that clips to the glass and sucks the oily film off the top of the water into a sponge. It runs on its own pump, so it does not need to be plumbed into your filter.
highlights: Clears surface film for better gas exchange
Sponge catches the debris, rinse and reuse
bestFor: Planted tanks up to 350 litres that get a stubborn protein film on the surface, which is common with CO2 and heavy feeding.
watchOut: It is a visible box in the tank, and the sponge needs rinsing often or it stops skimming.

name: EccoSkim
summary: A powered surface skimmer that pulls the oily film off the water surface. It clips straight onto a Juwel internal filter, sending the skimmed water into it, or mounts with suction cups in other glass tanks. A float keeps the inlet at the waterline as levels drop.
highlights: Clips onto Juwel Bioflow filters or mounts with suction cups
Floating inlet follows the water level
Clears surface film that blocks light and gas exchange
bestFor: Planted tanks, especially CO2 injected ones, that build up surface film.

specs.Mounting: Juwel filter mount or suction holder

watchOut: It sits inside the tank, so it adds another bit of kit to hide.

name: JY Surface Skimmer
summary: A small powered surface skimmer that draws the top layer of water through a floating intake to clear oily film. Two versions at 300 L/h.
bestFor: Planted tanks with surface film that blocks gas exchange and light.

name: Delta Mini Surface Skimmer
summary: A small stand-alone skimmer that pulls oily film and floating debris off the surface. The outlet sits below the waterline, so it clears the surface without splashing away the CO2 you are paying for.
highlights: Suits tanks of roughly 30 to 180 L
Works as a tiny extra filter as well as a skimmer
bestFor: CO2-injected planted tanks that keep getting a protein film on the surface.
watchOut: It is white and sits in the tank, so it is visible in a minimal layout.

name: FP Series Submersible Pump
summary: Slim internal pumps supplied with a perforated spray bar, so they can filter, circulate or feed a fountain. Four sizes from 300 to 1,350 L/h, with permanent-magnet motors and stainless shafts.
highlights: Spray bar included for even flow along the tank
bestFor: Adding gentle, spread-out circulation to a medium tank or powering a simple internal filter.

specs.Included: Spray bar outlet

watchOut: Spray bars sit high by design, so expect surface movement and some CO2 loss.

name: HL Crossflow Wave Pump
summary: A tube-shaped crossflow pump that pushes a wide sheet of water along the tank, a bit like a gyre, and can also aerate. It uses a DC variable-speed drive with a digital display. Sizes run from a 20 cm unit to a 70 cm bar for very large aquariums.
highlights: DC variable speed with LED display
Can aerate as well as circulate
bestFor: Long tanks where you want even flow across the whole front-to-back depth.
watchOut: Boyu does not publish flow figures, and the two big models draw 100 to 200 W.

name: PGB Series Submersible Pump
summary: Tall, narrow submersible pumps with a long intake tube, built to sit upright in a corner or on an undergravel uplift. Three sizes from 740 to 1,565 L/h with up to 2.4 m of head.
bestFor: Undergravel plates, sump returns or DIY top filters that need decent head in a narrow space.

name: SP-100 / SP-101 Series Powerhead
summary: A long-running range of small submersible powerheads with a venturi tube, a flow adjuster and an optional spray nozzle. Nine sizes run from a tiny 300 L/h unit to 1,850 L/h. Useful as a return pump, for driving an undergravel plate or just adding surface movement.
highlights: Venturi air injection and adjustable flow
bestFor: Anyone needing a cheap general-purpose pump for circulation, a DIY filter or a small sump return.
watchOut: The venturi and spray bar add a lot of surface agitation, which is not what you want on a CO2-injected tank.

name: SP-1000 Series Submersible Pump
summary: Compact multi-purpose submersible pumps that can push water, drive a fountain outlet or power a small filter. Five sizes from 300 to 1,400 L/h, with stainless steel shafts and resin-potted motors.
highlights: Up to 2 m head on the largest
Works as pump, fountain or filter pump
bestFor: Small sump returns, DIY filters and general water moving jobs around the fish room.
watchOut: Power use is on the high side for the flow on the bigger models (34 W for 1,400 L/h).

name: WM Series Wavemaker
summary: Round-bodied flow pumps that throw a broad, turbulent stream rather than a narrow jet, on a swivelling mount. The range covers single pumps (WM-101, WM-1, WM-2, WM-15), a 24 V magnet-mount WM-25, and multi-pump kits with a wave controller (WM-3 and WM-4).
highlights: Swivel mount points the flow any direction
WM-3 and WM-4 kits add a wave timer controller
WM-25 runs on DC 12 to 24 V, 5,500 L/h
bestFor: Medium and large planted tanks with dead spots behind hardscape, where you want circulation without a blasting jet.

specs.Mounting: Suction cup / rim bracket, adjustable angle

watchOut: Boyu only gives flow for the WM-25; the others are rated by tank size, and the marketing leans towards marine use.

name: WM-50 / WM-102 DC Wavemaker
summary: DC-driven wavemakers with an external digital controller that stores custom wave and flow programmes. WM-102 is a twin-pump set; WM-50 is a single, much stronger pump. Both run on a safe 24 V supply.
bestFor: Large tanks where you want adjustable, pulsed circulation from a controller.
watchOut: These are very strong pumps; most planted tanks will run them well below maximum.

name: AA Series Submersible Pump
summary: Grey and blue submersible pumps with a carry handle on the bigger sizes, running from 300 to 4300 L/h. Sold as "power liquid filter" pumps, they are general-purpose water movers.
highlights: Up to 4 m head on the AA9000
bestFor: A sump return or water-transfer pump where you need decent head height for the money.
watchOut: Power draw is high on the big models (116 to 125 W for AA6000 and AA9000); an efficient DC pump costs more upfront but less to run.

name: ECO DC Variable Pump
summary: A 24 V DC pump with a digital remote that gives 20 steps of steady flow, two wave modes and a feed pause. It also cuts out and alarms if it runs dry.
highlights: 20-step flow control plus fast and slow wave modes
bestFor: A sump return on a large tank where turning the flow down precisely matters more than raw price.

specs.Motor: 24 V DC, accepts 100 to 240 V AC input

watchOut: Even at its lowest setting it is a big pump, sized for large systems rather than a normal planted tank.

name: P Series Submersible Pump
summary: A long-running range of grey and black submersible pumps from 320 to 3000 L/h with a blue flow dial on the smaller models.
highlights: Flow adjustment dial on small and mid sizes
bestFor: Driving a DIY filter, a sump return or a water-change setup on a budget.
watchOut: The large models draw 66 to 88 W, which is a lot for a pump running around the clock.

name: P-608 / P-908 Power Head
summary: A classic square aquarium powerhead, the same pump used on Dophin top filters. Fitted with its sponge it doubles as a basic internal filter.
highlights: Can run a top filter or undergravel setup
Sponge attachment shown on the box
bestFor: Driving a top filter or giving an old-school tank extra flow.
watchOut: At 16 to 29 W these are thirsty next to modern DC circulation pumps.

name: PC Series Submersible Pump
summary: Compact square submersible pumps from 300 to 5000 L/h. The three largest get a carry handle and a flow controller.
highlights: Up to 3 m head on the largest
Flow controller on PC-3000, PC-4000, PC-5000
bestFor: A return pump for a sump, a DIY filter or water changes, sized to your head height.
watchOut: Watts climb steeply on the bigger models (120 W for the PC-5000), so check running cost if it will run all day.

name: PH Series Submersible Pump
summary: Small black submersible pumps from 300 to 1250 L/h, the sort used to drive a small filter, a paludarium stream or a spray.
bestFor: A small paludarium water feature, a DIY sponge or box filter, or topping up from a bucket.
watchOut: Head figures are the maximum lift with zero flow, so size up if you need to push water more than a metre.

name: WP Wave Pump
summary: A compact circulation pump on a suction-cup mount that tilts 100 degrees and swivels 360. Two sizes, rated 2000 and 5000 L/h.
bestFor: Adding gentle circulation to a larger planted tank to move CO2 and nutrients into dead spots.

specs.Mount: Suction cup, 100 degree tilt, 360 degree rotation

watchOut: It gives steady flow only, no wave controller, and the WP-3000 can be too strong for tanks under about 200 litres.

name: compactON
summary: compactON is a family of small, quiet water pumps for moving water around a tank, a sump or a DIY filter. The smaller ones stick to the glass with suckers, and most sizes have a flow dial.
highlights: Adjustable flow on all but the 5000
2100 and up can run outside the water as well
bestFor: Return pumps for sumps, DIY filters or water features in a planted setup.
watchOut: Output drops quickly with head height, so check the pump curve if you are lifting water a long way.

name: streamON+
summary: streamON+ is a compact propeller pump on a magnetic mount, used to push water around the tank rather than through a filter. It swivels on a ball joint and has a slider to throttle the outflow, and it is very frugal with power.
highlights: Magnet mount, easy to move and angle
bestFor: High-tech planted tanks that need extra circulation to push CO2 and nutrients into dense stem groups.
watchOut: Even the smallest moves a lot of water, so on a nano or with delicate fish, start on the lowest setting and aim it at the glass.

name: Universal
summary: The Universal pumps are the long-running workhorses of the Eheim range, used in sumps, trickle filters and fish houses. They can sit in the water or outside it, and a built-in prefilter protects the impeller.
highlights: Run submerged or inline outside the tank
bestFor: Sump returns or external plumbing on larger planted systems where you want a very durable pump.
watchOut: The bigger sizes draw 65 to 80 W, far more than a modern DC pump of similar output.

name: OptiMax
summary: A range of adjustable water pumps from 300 to 5,000 L/h, for circulation, running a DIY filter or returning water from a sump. The smaller models are submersible only, while the 800 and up can also run dry outside the tank. Flow is adjustable on every model.
highlights: 800 and larger can be installed dry (inline) or submerged
bestFor: Sump returns, DIY filters, water changes or extra circulation in a larger planted tank.
watchOut: The 2000 and up draw 30 to 80 W, which adds up on your bill and adds heat to the water if submerged.

name: CDP DC Frequency Pump
summary: A 24 V DC pump with an external controller, from 3,500 to 10,000 L/h. SunSun also sells the same pump as SDP and ZDP.
bestFor: Sump returns on mid to large tanks.

extra.Variants: CDP-3500B and CDP-3500W versions
CDP-6000B and CDP-6000W versions
CDP-10000B and CDP-10000W versions

name: CHJ Multi-Function Pump
summary: A broad range of AC pumps from 500 to 6,000 L/h. The CHJ-02 versions come with a filter column.
bestFor: Sump returns and powering filters on tanks of most sizes.

name: CTB Frequency Pump
summary: An efficient pump range from 2,500 to 7,000 L/h, suited to sumps and filter feeds. Six sizes.
bestFor: Mid to large sump returns.

name: CTP Frequency Pump
summary: A frequency pump range from 3,000 to 16,000 L/h, with low wattage for its flow. Twelve sizes.
bestFor: Sump returns on large tanks.

name: CW Wavemaker
summary: A 24 V propeller wavemaker with an external controller, from 4,000 to 20,000 L/h. Standard models are adjustable across a wide range; S models run at a fixed rate.
bestFor: Planted tanks from 50 cm up that need gentle, adjustable circulation.

name: HJ Mini Submersible Pump
summary: Tiny pumps from 200 to 800 L/h, used in desktop tanks, small fountains and DIY nano filters. The smallest are under 4 cm across.
bestFor: Nano tanks, all-in-one rear chambers and small DIY projects.

name: HJ Series Submersible Pump
summary: SunSun's HJ-500 to HJ-6000 pumps, a common choice as sump return pumps in its own cabinet tanks. Ten sizes from 500 to 6,800 L/h.
bestFor: Sump returns and closed-loop circulation on mid to large tanks.
watchOut: The large models are power hungry (150 W for the HJ-6000); a DC or frequency pump will cost less to run.

name: HJ-41 Series Submersible Pump
summary: A long-running line of compact AC submersible pumps from 400 to 3,000 L/h, with a round intake cover. Useful for powering a DIY filter, a return from a small sump or a water-change setup.
bestFor: Small sumps, DIY filters and general water moving.
watchOut: Older AC design, so power use is high for the flow on the bigger models; DC pumps are quieter and adjustable.

name: HQJ and CQJ Submersible Pump
summary: Small pumps from 350 to 1,600 L/h in several body styles, including 12 V DC versions (HQJ-D). The HQJ-500G and 700G are fitted to many SunSun tanks.
bestFor: Desktop and small tank filtration, rear chambers and top filters.

name: JDP DC Frequency Pump
summary: SunSun's popular 24 V DC return pump with a controller that steps flow through five levels on the bigger models. Seven sizes from 1,000 to 18,000 L/h; Q versions add a one-touch feed pause.
bestFor: Sump returns and closed loops where you want adjustable, quiet flow.

name: JGP Low Water Level Pump
summary: A bottom-intake pump with dry-run protection and a ceramic shaft, able to pump down to about 5 mm. Six sizes from 1,000 to 4,500 L/h.
bestFor: Water changes and draining tanks, shallow sumps.
watchOut: High wattage for the flow (130 W on the largest), so better for occasional jobs than 24/7 use.

name: JHP DC Pump
summary: A vertical 24 V DC pump from 2,000 to 6,000 L/h, with a slim cylindrical body. It fits tight sump sections.
bestFor: Sump returns where space is tight.

name: JP-06 Series Submersible Pump
summary: Multi-purpose AC pumps from 450 to 3,800 L/h with a boxy body and wide outlet sizes. Eight sizes.
bestFor: Sump returns and powering external filters on mid-size tanks.
watchOut: Power draw is high on the large models compared with SunSun's frequency pumps.

name: JP-G Series Submersible Pump
summary: Compact pumps from the 250 L/h JP-230G used in many SunSun desktop tanks, up to 1,800 L/h. GS versions trade a little head for more flow.
bestFor: Nano tank filters, small sumps and DIY builds.

name: JP-GL Low Water Level Pump
summary: A pump that can draw water down to about 5 mm, with a ceramic shaft and a 360 degree intake. Five sizes from 600 to 1,600 L/h.
highlights: Pumps down to about 5 mm of water
bestFor: Shallow sumps and emptying tanks during water changes.

name: JQP Submersible Pump and Filter
summary: An efficient compact pump range from 500 to 3,500 L/h, sold bare or with a filter column (JQP-F). Up to 3.6 m head.
bestFor: Sump returns and filter feeds on small to mid tanks.

specs.F models: The F models add a filter sponge on the intake so the pump works as a simple internal filter

name: JTP Frequency Pump
summary: Efficient frequency-controlled pumps from 1,800 to 5,800 L/h (including 12/24 V DC models) plus the smaller JTP-2000 to 3000. They move a lot of water for their wattage.
bestFor: Sump returns where running cost matters.

name: JTP-R Frequency Pump
summary: The larger JTP range, from 4,000 to 16,000 L/h, for big sumps and closed loops. Wattage stays reasonable for the flow.
bestFor: Large display tanks with a sump.
watchOut: Far too much flow for most planted tanks unless you are running a big sump.

name: JVP Wavemaker
summary: SunSun's classic magnet-mount wavemakers, from a tiny 2,000 L/h unit to the 24,000 L/h twin-head JVP-402. The head can be aimed, and several models rotate on the magnet.
bestFor: Adding circulation to large planted tanks so CO2 and nutrients reach every plant.
watchOut: Pick a small one for a planted tank; too much flow flattens stems and blows substrate around.

name: STP Eco Pump
summary: An efficient pump that works submerged or dry-mounted, from 3,000 to 8,000 L/h. The STP-3800 drives the barrel filters in SunSun's H3TS and HYTX-IT tanks.
bestFor: Sump returns and driving external pressure filters.

name: XDP DC Frequency Pump
summary: A Xiaoli-line 24 V DC pump from 1,000 to 6,800 L/h. S versions push harder against head.
bestFor: Sump returns and filter feeds on small to large tanks.

name: XGP Low Water Level Pump
summary: A pump with a thermal cut-out against running dry, a 360 degree intake and the ability to pump down to about 5 mm. Six sizes from 500 to 3,500 L/h.
bestFor: Water changes and shallow sumps.

name: XQP Submersible Pump
summary: Compact Xiaoli-line pumps in 500, 1,000 and 1,500 L/h, also sold with a filter box as XQP-F. Low wattage for the flow.
bestFor: Small sumps, rear-chamber tanks and DIY filters.

name: XVA Wave Pump
summary: A submersible wave pump for glass up to 12 mm, from 6,000 to 10,000 L/h. E versions differ in control.
bestFor: Circulation in tanks up to about a metre.

name: XVP Wavemaker
summary: A Xiaoli-line magnet-mount wavemaker in three sizes from 2,500 to 12,000 L/h.
bestFor: Circulation in mid to large tanks.

name: ZHL Low Water Level Pump
summary: A carry-handle pump with a 360 degree bottom intake and dry-run protection, from 1,000 to 4,500 L/h. SunSun also sells it as the CHL series.
bestFor: Water changes, tank moves and draining.
watchOut: Built for moving water rather than running quietly all day.

name: ZSP Frequency Pump
summary: A Zhizhen-line frequency pump from 2,500 to 14,000 L/h. Ten sizes, up to 7 m head.
bestFor: Sump returns on mid to large tanks.

name: ZZP Cross-Flow Wave Pump
summary: A long, gyre-style cross-flow pump (29 cm) that produces a wide sheet of flow, with a separate 24 V controller. One size for 70 to 120 cm tanks.
bestFor: Larger planted tanks where you want broad, even flow instead of a jet.

name: Sigma Water Pump
summary: Small submersible DC pumps with an adjustable flow dial. They are the return pumps UNS pairs with its all-in-one tanks, and they also work as a general-purpose pump in a sump or DIY build.
highlights: Four sizes from about 300 L/h to 1,500 L/h
Flow is adjustable on the pump
Low-voltage DC (5 V on the Sigma 5, 12 V on the others)
bestFor: Powering the rear chamber of an all-in-one tank, or a small custom filter or sump.
watchOut: Pick the size to match your tank's chamber; the listed flow drops quickly as head height goes up.

name: Vio Cube SBX Cabinet
summary: The matching cabinet for the Juwel Vio Cube 54. It matches the tank's 41 x 36 cm footprint exactly and lifts it to a comfortable viewing height, with a shelf inside for food and spares.
highlights: Made for the Vio Cube 54 footprint
Door and internal shelf for storage
Black or white to match the tank
bestFor: Vio Cube owners who want the tank freestanding at eye level rather than on existing furniture.

name: ScaperLine Cabinet
summary: The base cabinet from the ScaperLine set, sold on its own. It sits flush with the ScaperLine 100 tank and has the scaper-friendly details: a pull-out shelf for an external filter, a magnetic tool holder, towel holder and a sealable cable channel.
highlights: Sized to sit flush under the ScaperLine 100 aquarium
Pull-out shelf for an external filter
Magnetic holder for scissors and tweezers, plus a towel rail
Optional back panel turns it into a room divider
bestFor: Anyone buying a ScaperLine 100 tank separately, or replacing the cabinet.
watchOut: It is made for the ScaperLine 100 footprint, so check dimensions before using it with another tank.

name: Small Aquarium Cabinet
summary: A plain storage cabinet sized to fit under SunSun's small HE, HEK and HSJ tanks. It stands 80 cm tall on 2 cm feet, with a hidden cupboard for food, scissors and test kits.
bestFor: Anyone putting a small SunSun tank on a stand instead of a desk.
watchOut: Sized for specific SunSun tanks; check your tank's footprint before buying.

name: Aluminium Aquarium Stand
summary: An aluminium cabinet for the larger UNS tanks, borrowed from the brand's reef systems. There are no steel hinges to rust; the doors are magnetic and lift off completely, which makes working on a filter or CO2 setup inside much easier.
highlights: Fully removable magnetic doors (3 to 5 depending on size)
bestFor: Large planted tanks where rust-free construction and full access to the cabinet matter.

specs.Included: Levelling feet, anti-scratch bumper pads, assembly hardware

watchOut: It needs assembling, and it costs noticeably more than the wooden stands.

name: Aquarium Tank Stand
summary: Pre-assembled wooden cabinets sized to match UNS tanks exactly, from the 30C cube up to the 180U. Each has a soft-close door and cut-outs in the sides and back for hoses and cables, with enough room inside for a canister and a CO2 cylinder.
highlights: Sixteen sizes matched to UNS cube, U, P and L tanks
Four finishes: Oak, Natural Wood Grain, Jet Black and Piano White
Side and rear openings for filter tubing and CO2 line
bestFor: A UNS tank owner who wants a stand that matches the footprint to the centimetre.

specs.Finishes: Oak, Natural Wood Grain, Jet Black, Piano White

watchOut: The finish is water resistant, not waterproof, so wipe up drips and spills promptly.

name: Submersible UV Steriliser
summary: A UVC lamp in a quartz sleeve that sits inside the tank or sump rather than inline on a hose. Six sizes from 4 to 20 W.
highlights: Goes directly in the tank or sump
bestFor: Knocking out a green water bloom or running in a sump on a larger system.
watchOut: An open UV lamp in the display tank needs care, and it will not fix the nutrient imbalance behind an algae bloom.

name: Doctor 5
summary: Chihiros' latest electrolytic water-care unit. A reactor in the tank produces short-lived oxidisers to hold back algae and harmful bacteria, while the controller also watches temperature and shows it on a small screen and in the app.
highlights: Three modes; you enter your tank size during setup
Temperature monitoring with app and on-screen alerts
Maker states it is safe for fish, shrimp and filter bacteria
bestFor: Freshwater planted tanks where you want algae prevention and a temperature alarm in one small gadget.
watchOut: Only for water under 500 ppm TDS, and the reactor is a consumable that needs replacing.

name: Doctor Mate
summary: The small Doctor, sized for nano and small tanks up to about 125 L. It runs the same three plant, fish and shrimp modes as the larger unit, with Bluetooth control.
bestFor: Nano and small planted tanks, including shrimp tanks, that want an algae and bacteria hedge.
watchOut: Replacement reactors are an ongoing cost.

name: New Doctor
summary: The standard-size Chihiros Doctor, an electrolytic unit with separate plant, fish and shrimp modes. The plant mode targets algae, and the fish and shrimp modes aim at harmful bacteria. It comes with either Bluetooth app control or touch buttons.
highlights: Reactor sits on the glass, controller outside
Suited to tanks from about 75 L up
bestFor: Mid-size and larger planted tanks where you want an extra tool against algae alongside good maintenance.

specs.Tank size: About 20 to 30 US gal (75 to 115 L) and up

watchOut: It won't fix a light or nutrient imbalance, and the reactor needs periodic replacement.

name: reeflexUV
summary: reeflexUV is an inline UV clarifier that goes on your canister's return hose. A reflector inside bounces the UV back through the water, so it gets more done per watt than a plain unit, and it kills free-floating algae that turns water green.
highlights: Fits inline on the filter return
Internal reflector boosts effective UV dose
Clears green water from suspended algae
Three sizes to match tank volume and filter flow
bestFor: Planted tanks prone to green water, or anyone wanting a bit of extra clarity and pathogen control.
watchOut: It does nothing for algae growing on plants or glass, and the lamp needs replacing about once a year.

name: reeflexUV+e
summary: The reeflexUV+e is the WiFi version of the reeflexUV. You can run it constantly, on a daily schedule or linked to other Eheim devices, and it tells you by e-mail when the lamp is due for a change.
highlights: Constant, daily cycle or coupled modes over WiFi
Booster mode for a short, intense treatment
Switches off automatically when you open it to change the lamp
bestFor: Larger planted tanks where you want UV only for set hours, or want it tied into an Eheim digital setup.
watchOut: It costs about twice as much as the standard reeflexUV for the same job, so only worth it if you will use the scheduling.

name: ClearTronic
summary: An inline UV-C clarifier that plumbs into your filter outlet hose and clears green water and free-floating bacteria. The ballast is built into the body, so there is no separate box to find room for in the cabinet. The lamp and quartz sleeve come out with a quick-release for cleaning.
highlights: 7, 9 or 11 W UV-C for tanks up to 250, 400 or 600 litres
Quick-release for lamp changes and quartz cleaning
bestFor: Canister-filtered tanks prone to green water, or keepers who want an extra safeguard against outbreaks.
watchOut: UV lamps lose strength over time and need replacing roughly yearly, and UV does not fix the nutrient or light imbalance behind algae.

name: AUV UV-C Lamp
summary: A submersible UV-C lamp that sits in the tank or sump, from 3 to 14 W, rated for 500 to 2,600 litres. Most sizes come with a shade to block visible glare.
highlights: Rated for up to 500 to 2,600 litres
Light shield on 6 W and up
bestFor: Tanks or sumps with green water or where you want to cut free-floating bacteria.
watchOut: UV-C can harm eyes and degrade some plastics; never look at the lit lamp and keep it shielded.

name: ZUV Timer UV-C Lamp
summary: A submersible UV-C lamp with a built-in timer, from SunSun's Zhizhen line, rated for 1,800 to 2,600 litres. Three sizes, 10 to 14 W.
highlights: Rated for up to 1,800 to 2,600 litres
bestFor: Large tanks and sumps with green water.
watchOut: Keep the lamp shielded and switched off when your hands are in the tank.

name: Nano Sterilizer / Algae Inhibitor
summary: Twinstar's electrolytic steriliser: a small controller outside the tank powers a reactor disc on the glass that produces short-lived oxidising radicals. The idea is to knock back algae spores and bacteria before they take hold, without a UV lamp or plumbing into the filter.
highlights: Four sizes: M3, M5, Nano and Nano Plus
Reactor mounts inside the tank, no filter plumbing
Maker states it is safe for fish, shrimp, plants and filter bacteria
Best started on a new tank before algae appears
bestFor: Planted tanks up to about 250 L where you want an extra hedge against green water and algae, especially during the first months.

specs.Install: Reactor disc on glass, controller outside the tank

watchOut: It supports, not replaces, balanced light, CO2 and nutrients, and the reactor disc needs replacing and descaling over time.
